# ProGPU WPF Port Worklog

## 2026-06-14

- Created WPF integration branch `progpu-rendering-port`.
- Added ProGPU as a submodule at `external/ProGPU`, tracking `fix/render-invalidation-and-leaks`.
- Added `external/Directory.Build.props` and `external/Directory.Build.targets` so submodule projects do not inherit the WPF Arcade SDK imports from the superproject.
- Added `src/ProGPU.Wpf`, a cross-platform port lane for ProGPU-backed WPF rendering.
- Added `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget` and `ProGpuWpfWindowHost`.
- Added `IWpfCompositionCommandSink` and `ProGpuCompositionCommandSink` as the first DUCE/MIL replacement seam.
- Added `WpfMilRenderDataDecoder` for primitive generated WPF `RenderData` records:
  - line
  - rectangle
  - rounded rectangle
  - ellipse
  - geometry
  - image
  - glyph run
  - clip
  - opacity
  - opacity mask
  - transform
  - pop
- Added `WpfMilResourceRegistry` for WPF's one-based dependent resource token convention.
- Added `WpfResourceResolver` to adapt common real-WPF-shaped media resources to ProGPU shim types during `RenderData` replay.
- Added `IWpfImageSourceAdapter` and `WpfBitmapSourceImageAdapter` so WPF-shaped 32-bit `BitmapSource` pixels can be copied into ProGPU-backed `WriteableBitmap` instances when a replay caller opts into image upload.
- Added native ProGPU vector brush wrapping so WPF-shaped linear and radial gradient brushes can replay through the existing WPF `Brush` abstraction.
- Extended `WpfResourceResolver` geometry adaptation to cover WPF-shaped line geometry, ellipse geometry, and geometry groups in addition to rectangle/path geometry.
- Extended WPF-shaped `GeometryGroup` adaptation to preserve group fill rule and bake child geometry transforms into copied path figures.
- Extended WPF-shaped `PathGeometry` reflection adaptation to preserve figures, fill rule, line/polyline, quadratic/polyquadratic bezier, cubic/polycubic bezier, and arc segment metadata.
- Added WPF-shaped `CombinedGeometry` reflection adaptation, preserving union/intersect/xor/exclude boolean intent as ProGPU combined vector paths.
- Added `IWpfDrawingResourceResolver` and reflection replay for `MilDrawDrawing`, covering WPF-shaped `GeometryDrawing` and simple `DrawingGroup` resources.
- Added `WpfRenderDataBridge` to snapshot WPF `RenderData` private buffers and dependent resources, then replay them through the decoder.
- Added `WpfVisualContentBridge` to extract `DrawingVisual._content` and replay `RenderData` content through the same bridge.
- Added `WpfVisualTreeRenderer` for limited recursive visual subtree replay with transform, offset, clip, and opacity support.
- Added `WpfVisualInvalidationTracker` to observe WPF-shaped visual/resource `Changed`, `Invalidated`, `INotifyPropertyChanged`, and `INotifyCollectionChanged` signals and mark the ProGPU retained root dirty.
- Added retained `ProGPU.Scene.Visual.ChangeVersion` counters that advance on property invalidation, child invalidation propagation, and child collection changes, while render-time dirty clearing leaves the version stable.
- Fixed ProGPU `RenderOffscreen(...)` to compile visuals with a render-only offset override instead of mutating `Visual.Offset`, preserving `ChangeVersion` stability while native effect/layer rendering targets padded offscreen textures.
- Exposed `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.SceneChangeVersion`, `RetainedWpfChangeVersion`, and `FlatDrawingChangeVersion`, and changed WPF source invalidation to dirty the retained WPF root as well as the scene and flat drawing roots.
- Moved arc stroke shader parameter construction into public `ProGPU.Vector.ArcShaderParameters`/`ArcSegmentGeometry.TryCreateShaderParameters(...)`, so WPF-shaped arcs can use a stable ProGPU native shader ABI for transformed ellipse axes instead of compositor-private math.
- Added `IWpfRenderScheduler` and `CoalescingWpfRenderScheduler` as the first MediaContext-style render request boundary for the Silk.NET host.
- Routed visual-level transform and clip replay through `WpfResourceResolver` so WPF-shaped matrix transforms and rectangle/path geometry clips are adapted consistently with `RenderData` resources.
- Added `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.ReplayVisualSubtree` and `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.WpfRootVisual` to connect reflected WPF visual replay to the Silk.NET/WebGPU frame path.
- Threaded optional image-source upload through `WpfRenderDataBridge`, `WpfVisualContentBridge`, `WpfVisualTreeRenderer`, and `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget`.
- Enabled `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` to use `WpfBitmapSourceImageAdapter` by default for transition visual replay, while still allowing callers to replace or disable the adapter.
- Wired `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` root changes, resize, load, and ProGPU target invalidations into the coalescing render scheduler.
- Added WPF-shaped `GlyphRun` adaptation for MIL `DrawGlyphRun` and reflected `GlyphRunDrawing`, preserving glyph indices, baseline origin, font size, advance widths, and glyph offsets through the ProGPU glyph-run command path.
- Added ProGPU sink push-stack tracking for native opacity-mask scopes so decoded WPF `PushOpacityMask` records emit matching `PushOpacityMask`/`PopOpacityMask` render commands.
- Stored the active WPF transform on native opacity-mask commands so transformed visual and drawing mask scopes replay correctly in ProGPU.
- Added reflected `DrawingGroup.OpacityMask` replay when the mask brush can be adapted and the drawing exposes finite bounds.
- Added bounded visual-level `OpacityMask` replay when a reflected visual exposes usable bounds, content bounds, render size, or actual size.
- Replaced the ProGPU sink's default rectangular clip fallback with native `PushGeometryClip`/`PopGeometryClip` command emission for path-convertible WPF clip geometries.
- Replaced the ProGPU sink's default shim geometry draw path with native `DrawPath` command emission for path-convertible WPF geometries, preserving untransformed arc metadata.
- Extended native path conversion so translated, rotated/uniformly scaled, and axis-aligned positively scaled WPF arc segments remain ProGPU arc segments instead of degrading to endpoint lines.
- Replaced the ProGPU sink's primitive line, rectangle, rounded-rectangle, and ellipse draw paths with direct native `RenderCommand` emission carrying the active WPF transform.
- Replaced shim-compatible bitmap image drawing with direct native `DrawTexture` command emission carrying the active WPF transform.
- Replaced shim-compatible glyph-run drawing with direct native `DrawGlyphRun` command emission carrying the glyph-run transform composed with the active WPF transform.
- Replaced shim-compatible formatted text drawing with direct native `DrawText` command emission carrying the active WPF transform.
- Replaced shim opacity-scope handling with direct native `PushOpacity`/`PopOpacity` command emission.
- Added initial balance-only guideline-scope replay for `MilPushGuidelineSet`, `MilPushGuidelineY1`, and `MilPushGuidelineY2` so WPF render-data push/pop balance is preserved.
- Added reflected `DrawingGroup.GuidelineSet` replay as a matching no-op guideline scope around children.
- Added reflected visual snapping guideline replay as a matching no-op guideline scope around visual content and children.
- Added reflected visual `ScrollableAreaClip` replay as a rectangular clip scope around visual content and children.
- Added explicit unsupported-state accounting for reflected visual effects, bitmap effects, cache mode, edge mode, then-unsupported bitmap scaling, ClearType, and text rendering or hinting modes so transition replay does not silently drop those WPF visual states.
- Hardened reflected `DrawingGroup` replay so non-adaptable transform/clip state and then-unsupported effect/cache state skip the drawing group instead of replaying children with incorrect visual state.
- Split reflected drawing replay results into applied, skipped, and unsupported states so decoded `MilDrawDrawing` records report unsupported drawing resources separately from unresolved resource tokens.
- Added `IWpfPlatformServices` and default unsupported service implementations as the initial Win32 abstraction boundary.
- Added `CrossPlatformWpfPlatformServices` and `ProcessWpfLauncher` so the Silk.NET host has a portable `ShellExecute` replacement for URI and file launch requests.
- Added `ProcessWpfClipboard` so the Silk.NET host has a cross-platform clipboard service behind `IWpfClipboard` using `pbcopy`/`pbpaste`, PowerShell `Set-Clipboard`/`Get-Clipboard`, or Linux `wl-copy`/`wl-paste` with `xclip`/`xsel` fallbacks.
- Added `ProcessWpfFileDialogService` so the Silk.NET host has a cross-platform file open, file save, and folder picker service behind `IWpfFileDialogService` using `osascript`, PowerShell Windows Forms dialogs, or `zenity`.
- Added `SilkNetWpfMonitorService` so the Silk.NET host can enumerate monitor bounds and primary monitor identity without Win32 monitor APIs.
- Added `IWpfInputService` and `SilkNetWpfInputService` so the Silk.NET host exposes normalized key, text, mouse, and wheel events without depending on Win32 messages.
- Added `IWpfWindowEventService` and `SilkNetWpfWindowEventService` so the Silk.NET host exposes activation/deactivation and external file-drop events without depending on Win32 window messages.
- Added `IWpfTimerService`/`IWpfTimer` and `ThreadPoolWpfTimerService` so the port lane has a cross-platform timer boundary for future MediaContext, animation, hover, and scheduling work without Win32 timers.
- Added `IWpfViewport3DCommandSink` and `WpfViewport3DSceneBridge` so reflected WPF-shaped `Viewport3DVisual` content can compile into ProGPU's `Mesh3D` compositor extension payload.
- Added reflected Viewport3D support for projection cameras, `ModelVisual3D`, `Model3DGroup`, `GeometryModel3D`, `MeshGeometry3D`, diffuse/specular/material-group color extraction, model transforms, directional/ambient light hints, generated mesh normals, and front/back material entries.
- Added `WpfViewport3DTextureCache`, owned by `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget`, to reuse and dispose Viewport3D offscreen color/MSAA/depth textures across replay frames.
- Routed `WpfVisualTreeRenderer` so `Viewport3DVisual.Children` stay inside the 3D bridge instead of being recursively treated as 2D visual children.
- Extended `ProGpuCompositionCommandSink` to emit `DrawExtension(CompositorBuiltInExtensions.Mesh3D)` followed by a transformed `DrawTexture` composite for WPF-shaped Viewport3D content when a context-backed texture cache is available.
- Added `WpfCompositionDrawingContext` as the first source-level command sink adapter for managed WPF draw calls that should bypass `RenderData.WriteDataRecord` and write directly to `IWpfCompositionCommandSink`.
- Added stack-depth tracking and close-time auto-pop behavior to the source-level adapter to match `RenderDataDrawingContext.EnsureCorrectNesting`.
- Added source-level drawing-context operation counters and explicit unsupported `DrawVideo`/`PushEffect` hooks so generator redirection can report unsupported operations without silently dropping them.
- Added `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.OpenCompositionDrawingContext` and `CreateCompositionDrawingContext` so source-level managed draw calls can write into a ProGPU frame through `WpfCompositionDrawingContext`.
- Added `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.WpfDraw` and `LastSourceDrawingResult` so the Silk.NET host can run source-level managed WPF drawing callbacks during each frame before lower-level ProGPU draw callbacks.
- Added `src/ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` with focused decoder tests.
- Added GPU-free integration coverage that decodes WPF-shaped records through `ProGpuCompositionCommandSink` into real `ProGPU.Scene.RenderCommand` output.
- Added GPU-free Viewport3D reflection coverage for WPF-shaped mesh payload compilation and replay routing.
- Added GPU-free source-level drawing-context adapter coverage for direct managed draw forwarding, push/pop balancing, unsupported video/effect accounting, and unsupported push-scope balance.
- Added GPU-free host callback coverage for source-level draw invocation, result capture, close-time auto-pop, and no-callback reset behavior.
- Documented the initial architecture and ADR in `reports/`.
- Verified with `dotnet build src/ProGPU.Wpf/ProGPU.Wpf.csproj` from the project directory using the local net10 SDK boundary.
- Verified with `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Wpf.Tests/ProGPU.Wpf.Tests.csproj --verbosity minimal`.

- Added `QueuedWpfDispatcherService`, preserving owner-thread callback processing, WPF-shaped priority order, FIFO behavior within a priority, and pending-operation cancellation.

- Added GPU-free decoder coverage for WPF-shaped translate/scale transform groups, centered rotate transforms, and centered skew transforms without `Value` matrices.
- Extended the ProGPU vector radial-gradient brush, GPU brush packing, and WGSL gradient evaluation to carry separate X/Y radii plus gradient-origin/focal-point coordinates, then changed the WPF-shaped radial-gradient adapter to preserve `RadiusX`, `RadiusY`, and `GradientOrigin` instead of collapsing them to a larger circular radius centered at `Center`.
- Added ProGPU gradient spread-method support for `Pad`, `Reflect`, and `Repeat`, packed it into the GPU brush layout, applied it in the vector and hatch WGSL gradient paths, and mapped WPF-shaped gradient `SpreadMethod` values in the reflection resolver.
- Added WPF gradient `MappingMode` preservation for reflected gradient brushes and command-sink materialization of `RelativeToBoundingBox` linear/radial gradients against finite rectangle, rounded-rectangle, ellipse, geometry, line, pen, and opacity-mask bounds before recording ProGPU commands. Explicit `MappingMode=Absolute` gradients keep their source coordinates.
- Added WPF gradient `Transform` and `RelativeTransform` preservation for reflected gradient brushes. Linear and radial gradients now map finite-bounds coordinates first, then carry adaptable invertible 2D affine brush transforms as inverse ProGPU brush-coordinate transforms so the shader samples transformed brush space, including non-axis-aligned radial-gradient transforms.
- Added optional command-sink diagnostics sampled by `WpfMilRenderDataDecoder`, and wired `ProGpuCompositionCommandSink` to count non-invertible reflected gradient transforms, unrecognized reflected gradient `ColorInterpolationMode` values, and reflected gradient stop-table overflow above 65,536 stops as unsupported state when replay must fall back.
- Changed WPF-shaped gradient adaptation to preserve reflected valid gradient stops in the ProGPU vector brush up to the current 65,536-stop table capacity instead of trimming at the old fixed brush ABI boundary.
- Added ProGPU gradient color-interpolation support for WPF `SRgbLinearInterpolation` and `ScRgbLinearInterpolation`, carrying the mode through vector brushes, `GpuBrush`, vector WGSL, and hatch WGSL. The scRGB path converts sRGB stop colors to linear light for interpolation and converts the interpolated RGB result back to sRGB for output.
- Expanded ProGPU's `GpuBrush` ABI, vector brushes, vector WGSL, and hatch WGSL with a two-row affine brush-coordinate transform so transformed WPF linear and radial gradients are evaluated in shader space instead of CPU-flattening endpoints or radii.
- Moved ProGPU gradient stop sampling out of the fixed brush color slots and into a `GpuGradientStop` storage table shared by dynamic vector rendering, static DXF buffers, and hatch rendering. `GpuBrush` now stores a stop-table offset/count, vector group 0 binds the stop table, and the hatch extension binds the same table at its group 0 binding 4.
- Added basic ProGPU sink Y-guideline snapping for generated `PushGuidelineY1` and `PushGuidelineY2` scopes on axis-aligned primitive line, rectangle, rounded-rectangle, and ellipse coordinates; the `PushGuidelineY2` path snaps the leading coordinate and preserves the driven-edge offset.
- Added GPU-free coverage for Y-guideline snapping through decoded MIL records and for preserving unsnapped coordinates under rotated transforms.
- Added `IWpfCompositionCommandSink.PushGuidelineSet(object?)`, typed portable dynamic guideline-set transport, and optional `IWpfGuidelineSetResourceResolver` support so dynamic frozen `GuidelineSet` X/Y arrays can reach the ProGPU sink from source-level drawing and MIL dependent-resource replay.
- Extended ProGPU primitive guideline snapping to both X and Y axes for dynamic `GuidelineSet` scopes on axis-aligned line, rectangle, rounded-rectangle, and ellipse commands.
- Added GPU-free coverage for dynamic `GuidelineSet` pass-through and decoded MIL `PushGuidelineSet` X/Y primitive snapping.

Off Windows, `JpegBitmapDecoder`, `BitmapDecoder.Create(...)`, URI-backed decoder creation, and `BitmapImage(Uri)` now decode common JPEG bytes through `StbImageSharp`, convert RGBA output into WPF `Bgra32` frames, and bypass WIC for local seekable streams or filesystem URIs. The SDK supplies the `StbImageSharp` package/runtime asset so existing apps keep the same WPF imaging API shape after changing only the project `Sdk`.
- Verified the portable JPEG checkpoint with a clean Release `PresentationCore` build, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev` and `ProGPU.Wpf.Sdk.11.0.0-dev` packages, clean `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkExternalSmokeHarness` and `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` builds, a passing generated external SDK smoke run, focused `WpfManagedProjectGraphTests.RealPresentationFrameworkSmokeGuardsNativePlatformEntrypoints|WpfManagedProjectGraphTests.ProGpuWpfSdkProvidesSwitchOnlyPackagingSurface` coverage with 2 passed through `dotnet vstest`, and clean `git diff --check`.
- Added the first portable managed ICO decoder checkpoint for SDK-switched apps. Off Windows, `IconBitmapDecoder`, `BitmapDecoder.Create(...)`, URI-backed decoder creation, and `BitmapImage(Uri)` now recognize ICO containers with embedded PNG payloads, select the best PNG-backed directory entry, and reuse the existing managed `PngBitmapDecoder` to produce WPF `BitmapFrame` output. This covers a common application/window-icon format without introducing a parallel PNG codec; classic DIB/mask icon payloads remain a follow-up.
- Verified the PNG-backed ICO checkpoint with a clean Release `PresentationCore` build, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev` package, clean `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkExternalSmokeHarness` and `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` builds, a passing generated external SDK smoke run, focused `WpfManagedProjectGraphTests.RealPresentationFrameworkSmokeGuardsNativePlatformEntrypoints|WpfManagedProjectGraphTests.ProGpuWpfSdkProvidesSwitchOnlyPackagingSurface` coverage with 2 passed through `dotnet vstest`, and clean `git diff --check`.
- Expanded the portable managed ICO decoder to classic BI_RGB DIB icon payloads. The non-Windows `IconBitmapDecoder` now reads 1/4/8-bit palette entries, 24-bit BGR rows, 32-bit BGRA rows, bottom-up DIB storage, doubled ICO bitmap heights, and AND-mask transparency into WPF `Bgra32` frames, while still preferring the existing PNG payload path when present. The generated external SDK smoke now validates DIB-backed ICO stream and local-file decode from a normal SDK-switched app.
- Verified the DIB-backed ICO checkpoint with a clean Release `PresentationCore` build, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev` package, clean `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkExternalSmokeHarness` and `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` builds, a passing generated external SDK smoke run, focused `WpfManagedProjectGraphTests.RealPresentationFrameworkSmokeGuardsNativePlatformEntrypoints|WpfManagedProjectGraphTests.ProGpuWpfSdkProvidesSwitchOnlyPackagingSurface` coverage with 2 passed through `dotnet vstest`, and clean `git diff --check`.
- Revalidated the visible SDK-switch smoke offset against refreshed source-built mutable packages and clean package-mode output. The direct macOS apphost run configured the WebGPU swapchain at `840x1680`, and the capture at `/tmp/progpu-wpf-sdk-smoke-offset-check.png` showed the WPF client filling the visible smoke window. No render-path code change was needed in this checkpoint; the user screenshot matched stale `11.0.0-dev` package/output behavior rather than the current native-size normalization, retained-layer DPI scale, and explicit physical viewport path.
- Added a portable static GIF first-frame decoder path for SDK-switched apps. Off Windows, `GifBitmapDecoder`, `BitmapDecoder.Create(...)`, local URI-backed decoder creation, and `BitmapImage(Uri)` now recognize GIF signatures, decode the first frame through the SDK-supplied `StbImageSharp` package, convert RGBA to WPF `Bgra32`, and expose the result through the normal managed `BitmapFrame` APIs. Animation timing, multi-frame enumeration, palette/metadata fidelity, and download/cache behavior remain follow-up work.
- Extended managed WPF palette reuse off Windows. `BitmapPalettes.*` predefined palettes now initialize their managed `Colors` collections without WIC, `BitmapPalette(BitmapSource, maxColorCount)` can copy palette colors from managed indexed sources or extract unique colors from common BGRA/BGR/RGB managed bitmap sources, and `BitmapPalette.CreateFromBitmapSource(...)` returns the existing managed palette instead of forcing `WicSourceHandle`. The external SDK smoke validates predefined black/white, gray, and web palettes plus palette extraction from package-built `BitmapSource` instances.
- Added the first portable TIFF decoder checkpoint for SDK-switched apps. Off Windows, `TiffBitmapDecoder`, `BitmapDecoder.Create(...)`, local URI-backed decoder creation, and `BitmapImage(Uri)` now parse a baseline first IFD for uncompressed chunky 8-bit grayscale, RGB, and RGBA TIFF images into WPF `Bgra32` frames before WIC. The generated external SDK smoke validates stream, direct decoder, URI decoder, and `BitmapImage` TIFF paths from package-built output. Multi-page TIFF, compression schemes, orientation, metadata, color profiles, and tiled/planar storage remain follow-up codec work.
- Extended the portable PNG decoder to Adam7 interlaced images. The managed non-Windows `PngBitmapDecoder` now accepts `interlaceMethod=1`, inflates the pass stream once, unfilters each Adam7 pass with the existing PNG filter implementation, maps pass pixels back to the final WPF `Bgra32` frame, and keeps the normal non-interlaced path unchanged. The external SDK smoke now generates an interlaced RGBA PNG and validates stream, URI decoder, and `BitmapImage` paths from package-built output.

- Hardened the SDK smoke Retina/HiDPI startup path by synchronizing the portable `PresentationSource` DPI scale during Silk.NET native window load and resize, before the first render pass. `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` now caches the last resolved logical/physical `RenderSurfaceGeometry` and applies its DPI scale to the portable source immediately, keeping WPF layout in DIPs while the WebGPU swapchain stays physical. A local macOS direct SDK smoke run configured an `840x1680` swapchain and the capture `/tmp/progpu-wpf-sdk-smoke-after-dpi-sync.png` showed the current WPF client filling the visible smoke window; this hardening prevents first-frame or stale-package quadrant regressions from reappearing silently.

- Extended the portable TIFF decoder to uncompressed palette images. Off Windows, `TiffBitmapDecoder` now reads the TIFF `ColorMap` tag, supports packed 1/2/4/8-bit palette indices, expands the palette's 16-bit red/green/blue planes into WPF `Bgra32` pixels, and keeps the existing grayscale/RGB/RGBA first-frame path unchanged. The external SDK smoke generates a 4-bit palette TIFF and validates stream, direct decoder, URI decoder, and `BitmapImage(Uri)` paths from a package-built app with no ProGPU-specific code.

- Extended the portable TIFF decoder through multi-frame first-IFD-chain loading. `TiffBitmapDecoder` now follows `NextIfdOffset` links with cycle/count guards, builds a frozen `BitmapFrame` collection through WPF's normal `BitmapDecoder.Frames` API, and keeps `BitmapImage(Uri)` on the first frame. The generated external SDK smoke now creates a two-frame uncompressed TIFF and validates `BitmapDecoder.Create(...)`, direct `TiffBitmapDecoder`, and URI decoder frame counts plus second-frame pixels from a package-built app.

- Hardened the SDK smoke Retina/HiDPI startup path when Silk.NET or the current monitor service reports a usable physical framebuffer but a `1.0` monitor scale. `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` now keeps the existing monitor scale when it is greater than `1.0`, but on macOS reads the actual Cocoa window screen's `backingScaleFactor` before falling back to `NSScreen.mainScreen` and resolving the logical/physical render surface. This keeps WPF layout and the portable `PresentationSource` in DIPs while promoting the WebGPU swapchain to physical pixels. Verified with a clean `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` build, focused host/graph coverage through `dotnet vstest` with 5 passed, a refreshed `ProGPU.Wpf.11.0.0-dev` package, clean package-mode `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchSmoke` build, passing SDK-switch runtime and generated external SDK smoke runs, and a direct macOS apphost capture at `/tmp/progpu-wpf-sdk-smoke-backing-scale-fallback.png` after WebGPU configured the `420x840` DIP smoke window at an `840x1680` swapchain.

- Extended the portable GIF decoder through managed multi-frame enumeration. Off Windows, `GifBitmapDecoder`, `BitmapDecoder.Create(...)`, and local URI-backed decoder creation now parse GIF containers directly, including global/local color tables, graphic-control transparency and disposal, LZW image data, interlace, and composited full-canvas `Bgra32` `BitmapFrame` snapshots. The generated external SDK smoke now writes a deterministic two-frame GIF and validates stream, direct decoder, URI decoder, frame count, and second-frame pixels from package-built output; public animation timing metadata, cache/download behavior, and texture-backed frame reuse remain follow-up work.

- Extended portable image URI loading through WPF project `Resource` pack streams. Off Windows, the managed BMP/PNG/JPEG/ICO/GIF/TIFF decoder URI helpers now share `BitmapDecoder.TryOpenPortableUriStream(...)`, which can open filesystem, `pack://application:,,,/...`, and seekable/copied web streams before the path falls back to WIC. The generated external SDK app now embeds `Assets/ExternalImage.png` as a normal WPF resource and validates `BitmapDecoder.Create(packUri, ...)`, direct `PngBitmapDecoder(packUri, ...)`, and `BitmapImage(packUri)` from package-built output without app-side ProGPU code.

- Extended the SDK smoke through compiled XAML image resource loading. The generated package-built app now uses `Image.Source="Assets/ExternalImage.png"` and an `ImageBrush ImageSource="pack://application:,,,/Assets/ExternalImage.png"` in `MainWindow.xaml`, then validates the BAML-created `BitmapSource` dimensions, format, and pixels after normal `Application.Run()`. This keeps URI value serialization, BAML object creation, resource image lookup, and image/brush source ownership in managed WPF for SDK-switched apps.

- Fixed the live SDK smoke offset path where the ProGPU swapchain was correctly configured in physical Retina pixels but WPF's portable presentation source could keep measuring the root from stale declared window dimensions. `PortablePresentationSource` now exposes an internal `SetClientSize(double,double)` ABI that remeasures and arranges the root `UIElement` in WPF DIPs, `WpfPortablePresentationSourceBridge` reflects that ABI, and `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` synchronizes logical client size plus DPI scale from the resolved Silk.NET/ProGPU `RenderSurfaceGeometry` during load, resize, and render. This mirrors the layout-size role that `HwndSource` plays for classic WPF while keeping ProGPU presentation in physical framebuffer pixels.
- Verified the portable client-size fix with a clean `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major .dotnet/dotnet build src/ProGPU.Wpf.Tests/ProGPU.Wpf.Tests.csproj -v:minimal`, focused portable-source/host/drawing-frame/managed-graph coverage with 95 passed through `dotnet vstest`, a clean Release `PresentationCore` rebuild, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev` and signed `ProGPU.Wpf.11.0.0-dev` packages with assembly version `11.0.0.0`, and a passing generated external SDK smoke run that validates the shipped `PresentationCore.SetClientSize(double,double)` ABI before building the SDK-only app.

The SDK-only app now declares live-filtered, live-sorted, and live-grouped views over an `INotifyPropertyChanged` item collection with `IsLiveFilteringRequested`, `IsLiveSortingRequested`, `IsLiveGroupingRequested`, and live property lists, then mutates item properties and validates that WPF updates the bound `ListBox` views without a manual `Refresh()`. This keeps collection-view live filtering, sorting, and grouping in WPF's managed data-view manager for apps that only change project SDK.

- Fixed the current SDK smoke offset report by extending `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.ResolveLogicalClientSize(...)` for mixed macOS/Silk.NET startup sizing. When monitor DPI is still reported as `1.0`, the host now infers that native dimensions are already physical if they match cached WPF DIP dimensions multiplied by a plausible scale, even when `FramebufferSize` is larger again. This keeps the `420x840` WPF smoke window measured in DIPs while the ProGPU swapchain remains physical, preventing the white WPF content from staying in the upper-left half of the native window.
- Verified the mixed-size SDK smoke offset fix with a clean `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` build, focused host coverage for direct resolution and native resize cache preservation with 4 passed, focused project-graph coverage for the render-wakeup and SDK packaging guards with 2 passed, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev` and `ProGPU.Wpf.11.0.0-dev` packages, package inspection showing the new native-DPI inference helpers in `ProGPU.Wpf.dll`, clean package-mode `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchSmoke` build, passing `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchRuntimeHarness`, and passing generated external SDK smoke. - Advanced the tracked ProGPU submodule branch to `0ccd3e0` for two PR #17 review fixes that matter to WPF/Silk.NET rendering fidelity. The Skia shim now snapshots active clip pushes when `SaveLayer(...)` opens and replays them into offscreen layer rendering before image filters run, preventing blur/drop-shadow sampling from pixels outside the active clip. `ImageEffectExtensionPipeline` now queues cached texture bind groups, per-draw effect bind groups, bind-group layouts, and pipeline layouts through `WgpuContext` disposal queues instead of releasing WebGPU handles directly from teardown/prune paths. Added regression coverage with `SkCanvasStateTests.SaveLayerBlurImageFilterClipsOffscreenSourceBeforeFiltering` and `CompositorReviewRegressionTests.ImageEffectPipelineDisposeQueuesGpuHandles`, and replied on both PR review threads with the fix and validation details.
- Extended the portable GIF decoder through first public frame-control metadata. Portable non-Windows GIF frames now carry a read-only managed `BitmapMetadata` backing store for WIC-compatible frame queries such as `/grctlext/Delay`, `/grctlext/Disposal`, transparency state, and image descriptor fields. The generated no-source-change external SDK smoke validates stream, direct decoder, and URI decoder GIF frame-delay metadata from package-built output, keeping this in WPF's imaging API surface while full animation playback/cache behavior remains a follow-up.

- Fixed the current SDK smoke offset report by making the bound portable `PresentationSource` the logical-size authority after WPF attaches to the Silk.NET host. `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.SetClientSize(...)` now immediately synchronizes the source client size, and render/resize geometry resolves from the source's cached WPF DIP size before falling back to the host cache. This covers the observed Retina shape where native callbacks can temporarily cache physical dimensions while the WPF root should still measure at `420x840` DIPs and ProGPU should render into an `840x1680` physical target.
- Aligned the signed `ProGPU.Wpf` bridge package identity with the SDK transport contract by stamping `Version`/`PackageVersion=11.0.0-dev` and `AssemblyVersion`/`FileVersion=11.0.0.0` in its local build props. - Extended portable TIFF frame metadata through the public WPF `BitmapMetadata` query surface. The non-Windows `TiffBitmapDecoder` now reads IFD orientation tag 274, creates read-only portable `BitmapMetadata("tiff")`, and exposes `/ifd/{ushort=274}` as a boxed `ushort`, matching the typed query path expected by SDK-switched apps. The external SDK smoke validates stream, direct decoder, URI decoder, and direct-URI `TiffBitmapDecoder` metadata queries from package-built output.
- Verified this SDK smoke offset/package/TIFF checkpoint with clean `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` and `external/ProGPU` test builds, focused host/drawing-frame coverage with 5 passed, focused graph coverage with 2 passed, focused ProGPU compositor viewport coverage with 3 passed, clean Debug and Release `PresentationCore` builds, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev` and signed `ProGPU.Wpf.11.0.0-dev` packages, clean package-mode `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchSmoke` build, passing `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchRuntimeHarness`, and a passing generated external SDK smoke run.
- Completed the managed generic collection contracts for two `PresentationFramework` internals used by WPF item/control managers. `MS.Internal.ListOfObject` now forwards mutation, indexer, read-only, and removal operations to its wrapped `IList`, and `MS.Internal.WeakDictionary<TKey,TValue>` key/value collections now support `CopyTo`, value `Contains`, enumeration, and standard read-only `NotSupportedException` mutation failures instead of `NotImplementedException`. The generated external SDK smoke reflects both internal types from package-built `PresentationFramework.dll` and validates the contracts from an app that only selects `ProGPU.Wpf.Sdk`.
- Verified this managed-framework collection slice with clean Debug and Release `PresentationFramework` builds, clean `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkExternalSmokeHarness` and `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` builds, focused `WpfManagedProjectGraphTests.PresentationFrameworkInternalCollectionsImplementGenericContracts|WpfManagedProjectGraphTests.ProGpuWpfSdkProvidesSwitchOnlyPackagingSurface` coverage with 2 passed through `dotnet vstest`, clean `git diff --check`, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev`, and a passing generated external SDK smoke run.
- Fixed the live SDK smoke Retina offset path by splitting portable window startup sizing into two phases. `WpfPortableWindowActivation` now copies the initial WPF `Window.Title`, `WindowState`, and logical `Width`/`Height` into `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` during attach through `SetInitialClientSize(...)`, but defers `PortablePresentationSource.SetClientSize(...)` until `Show()`/`Run()` when WPF has completed portable activation. This keeps the smoke window measured as `420x840` DIPs while ProGPU/Silk.NET renders to the `840x1680` physical swapchain, and avoids the early `Window.GetWindowMinMax()` reentrancy hit seen when relayout was forced during attach.
- Fixed a package-mode clipboard state leak exposed after the SDK smoke startup fix. `PortableClipboardService` now treats managed portable clipboard state as authoritative after `Clipboard.Clear()` or any portable `Set*` call, clears the native text mirror when the current managed data object has no Unicode text, and resets that managed state when the active service registration is disposed. This prevents old process/native text from being rehydrated after a file-drop-only or cleared clipboard while keeping the initial native text fallback available before WPF owns the portable clipboard state.
- Verified this SDK smoke startup/clipboard checkpoint with a clean `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` build, focused host/activation/source/drawing-frame/managed-graph coverage with 119 passed through `dotnet vstest`, a clean Release `PresentationCore` build, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev` and signed `ProGPU.Wpf.11.0.0-dev` packages, clean package-mode `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchSmoke` build with only existing `NU1900` unavailable Azure vulnerability-feed warnings, passing `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchRuntimeHarness`, and passing generated external SDK smoke. A full `PresentationCore.Tests` build is still blocked in this macOS CLI environment by `DirectWriteForwarder.vcxproj` requiring Visual Studio C++ targets, although the managed `PresentationCore` project itself rebuilt cleanly.
- Fixed the SDK smoke offset path where a startup native resize could overwrite the host client cache with physical Retina dimensions before WPF's portable `PresentationSource` cache was bound. `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` now carries the requested logical client size from WPF `Window.Width`/`Height`, uses it before falling back to the native cache, and updates it only after normalized native resize resolution, keeping WPF layout in DIPs while ProGPU presents into the physical render target.
- Added the first portable routed drag/drop bridge for SDK-switched apps. `PortableWindowActivationService.ProcessDragDrop(...)` converts native host file/text payloads into a WPF `DataObject`, `DragDrop.ProcessPortableDrop(...)` reuses WPF's routed `PreviewDrop`/`Drop` event path and preserves the allowed-effect mask, and `WpfPortableWindowActivation` invokes that bridge before the older test/fallback file-drop hooks. The generated external SDK app now validates normal XAML `AllowDrop`, `PreviewDrop`, and `Drop` handlers from package-built output.
- Verified this SDK offset and routed drag/drop checkpoint with clean Release `PresentationCore` and `PresentationFramework` builds, a clean `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` build, focused host/activation/drawing-frame/managed-graph coverage with 150 passed through `dotnet vstest`, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev` and signed `ProGPU.Wpf.11.0.0-dev` packages, a passing generated external SDK smoke run, and a passing `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchRuntimeHarness` run.
- Extended the portable routed drag/drop bridge from final drop to the WPF drag lifecycle. `WpfDragDropEventKind` now carries `DragEnter`, `DragOver`, `DragLeave`, and `Drop`; `PortableWindowActivationService.ProcessDragDropEvent(...)` maps those kinds to WPF `DragDrop` routed events; `DragDrop.ProcessPortableDragDrop(...)` reuses WPF's preview/bubble event raising for all phases; and `WpfPortableWindowActivation` prefers that event-kind service before legacy drop-only fallback hooks. The generated external SDK app now validates `PreviewDragEnter`/`DragEnter`, `PreviewDragOver`/`DragOver`, `PreviewDragLeave`/`DragLeave`, and `PreviewDrop`/`Drop` from package-built output.
- Verified this portable drag/drop lifecycle checkpoint with clean Release `PresentationCore` and `PresentationFramework` builds, clean `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` build, focused activation/graph/platform drag-drop coverage with 61 passed through `dotnet vstest`, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev` and signed `ProGPU.Wpf.11.0.0-dev` packages, a passing generated external SDK smoke run, and a passing `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchRuntimeHarness` run.
- Extended the external SDK `Application.Run` lifetime gate through WPF managed window close semantics. The generated no-source-change SDK app now wires `Closing` and `Closed` from compiled `MainWindow.xaml`, cancels one `Window.Close()` and verifies the main window remains visible and present in `Application.Windows`, then switches to `ShutdownMode.OnMainWindowClose`, closes the main window for real, verifies final `Closing`/`Closed` sequencing, and lets WPF's managed shutdown path terminate the portable ProGPU/Silk.NET run loop.
- Extended the external SDK lifetime gate through a real secondary WPF window. During `Application.Run()`, the generated no-source-change app now opens a second `Window`, verifies it appears in `Application.Windows`, closes it while `ShutdownMode.OnLastWindowClose` is still active, verifies `Closing`/`Closed` fire and the secondary window is removed, and confirms the application has not exited while the main window remains open.
- Extended the external SDK lifetime gate through WPF owner/owned-window manager reuse. `Window.Owner` now accepts an already-active portable ProGPU/Silk.NET owner window instead of requiring an `HwndSource`, while leaving `SetOwnerHandle(...)` on the zero-handle path. The generated no-source-change app now creates an owned `Window` with `Owner = mainWindow`, verifies `OwnedWindows` membership and `Application.Windows` tracking, then closes the owner and verifies WPF closes the owned child even when the child's `Closing` handler attempts to cancel. This keeps ownership, owned-window collection updates, and parent-close cancellation policy in managed WPF.
- Added the first portable `Window.ShowDialog()` path for ProGPU/Silk.NET activation. `ShowDialog()` now branches before Win32 owner/window enumeration when the portable activation service is enabled, reuses WPF's managed `Show()`, modal dispatcher frame, `DialogResult`, `Closing`, and `Closed` paths, and lets source-null portable close stop the dialog frame through `DoDialogHide()` while skipping HWND re-enable/activation work. The external SDK smoke now opens an owned modal dialog, closes it by setting `DialogResult = true` from the dispatcher, and validates owner/`OwnedWindows`/`Application.Windows` state from package-built output.
- Fixed the visible SDK smoke Retina offset by hardening `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` logical-client cache reconciliation. When the portable `PresentationSource` cache and WPF-requested client size differ by a plausible DPI scale, the host now keeps the smaller DIP-sized value before resolving native Silk.NET resize geometry, preventing a transient `840x1680` physical source cache from replacing the intended `420x840` WPF layout size. Verified with focused host tests, graph coverage, a refreshed `ProGPU.Wpf.11.0.0-dev` package, a passing generated external SDK smoke run, and a direct macOS window capture at `/tmp/progpu-wpf-captures/sdk-smoke-window-after-offset-fix.png` showing the WPF client filling the smoke window.
- Added the portable `Window.Left`/`Window.Top` bridge for the ProGPU/Silk.NET host. `PortableWindowActivationService` now exposes a `SetPosition(...)` delegate, `Window.OnLeftChanged`/`OnTopChanged` branch to it when a portable activation is live while preserving the existing HWND path on Windows, and `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` carries nullable initial placement through `WindowOptions.Position` plus live `IWindow.Position` updates. This keeps WPF-owned placement properties, `_actualLeft`/`_actualTop`, and `LocationChanged` behavior in managed WPF while moving the native move operation behind Silk.NET instead of calling `SetWindowPos` off Windows.
- Verified this portable window-position checkpoint with clean Release `PresentationFramework` and Debug `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` builds, focused activation/host/managed-graph coverage with 83 passed through `dotnet vstest`, refreshed `Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.GitHub.11.0.0-dev` and signed `ProGPU.Wpf.11.0.0-dev` packages, and a passing generated external SDK smoke run that validates package-shipped `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.SetPosition(...)`, `PortableWindowActivationService.SetPosition(...)`, and normal SDK-built XAML `Left`/`Top` property updates.
- Added the portable `Window.Topmost` bridge beside the existing title, client-size, state, and position paths. `Window.OnTopmostChanged(...)` now forwards live topmost updates through `PortableWindowActivationService.SetTopmost(...)` when a ProGPU/Silk.NET activation is active, and `WpfPortableWindowActivation` copies initial `Topmost` state into `ProGpuWpfWindowHost`/Silk.NET `WindowOptions.TopMost`. The SDK runtime and external SDK harnesses now validate package-shipped topmost APIs and XAML `Topmost` mutation without requiring app code to call ProGPU.
- Fixed the portable `Application.Run()` idle-work handoff exposed by the generated external SDK app. `WpfPortableWindowActivation.Run()` now drains WPF dispatcher work through `DispatcherPriority.ApplicationIdle` before entering the blocking Silk.NET native loop, and returns without entering `Host.Run()` if that idle work closes and disposes the activation. This keeps startup validation, idle resource/style/control work, and no-source-change app shutdown on WPF's dispatcher instead of requiring a ProGPU-specific startup callback.
- Hardened the SDK smoke offset regression gate against stale fixed-version package output. Both the SDK switch runtime harness and generated external SDK smoke now inspect the resolved `ProGPU.Scene.Compositor` IL and require the physical `RenderScene(root,width,height,targetView)` path to call `ApplyRenderPassViewport(...)`, which must call Silk.NET WebGPU `RenderPassEncoderSetViewport(...)`. This makes the half-window Retina failure mode fail in package validation instead of depending on visual inspection, while WPF layout remains in DIPs and ProGPU presents to the physical swapchain.

- Added ProGPU submodule commit `f168dc2` for the latest PR #17 Avalonia-host staging-buffer review item. `ProGpuHostControl` now queues zero-copy swapchain and fallback custom-visual staging buffers through `WgpuContext.QueueBufferDisposal(...)` instead of destroying/releasing them directly during teardown or resize, so submitted copy/map work can drain before native buffer release. - Extended the runnable MVP SDK app through WPF `CompositeCollection` and `CollectionContainer` item composition. The Resources tab now declares a composite resource that mixes direct strings with a static observable collection, binds it to a normal `ItemsControl`, and the package-mode self-test validates flattened item order plus collection-change propagation through WPF's item/collection-view managers instead of adding a ProGPU-side item composition layer.

- Advanced the ProGPU submodule to `a53510c` (`Fix Skia hairline and path-op fill rules`) for the latest PR #17 Skia shim review threads. Skia zero-width strokes now map to a renderable hairline pen instead of disappearing as non-positive native thickness, and `SKPath.Op(...)` now propagates the solver's returned fill rule back to the wrapper path/result overload so even-odd path-op results keep their fill semantics. Added focused ProGPU regression coverage, replied to both active review comments, resolved those threads, and resolved the older outdated review threads that already had fix replies.
- Extended the runnable MVP SDK app through WPF mouse input bindings. `MainWindow.xaml` now declares a normal `MouseBinding` for `LeftDoubleClick` against the same routed command as the keyboard/menu path, and the package-mode self-test validates the compiled gesture, command parameter, command target, and routed execution. This keeps mouse gesture metadata and command routing in reused managed WPF while the ProGPU/Silk.NET host remains responsible for delivering native mouse events.
- Extended the runnable MVP SDK app through normal WPF `Canvas` and `Shape` controls. The Layout tab now includes compiled `Rectangle`, `Ellipse`, `Line`, and `Path` elements with attached canvas positions, stroke caps, fills, and parsed path geometry, and the package-mode self-test validates the shape metadata from SDK-built BAML. This gives the manually launchable MVP app a simple rendering-facing surface for ProGPU retained replay without adding app-side ProGPU APIs.
- Extended the runnable MVP SDK app through WPF common file/folder dialogs. The Controls tab now calls `Microsoft.Win32.OpenFileDialog`, owner `SaveFileDialog`, and owner `OpenFolderDialog` from normal app code, while the package-mode self-test scopes a deterministic `PortableFileDialogService` handler and validates request kind/title/filter/default-extension metadata plus selected path and safe-name state. This moves another common simple-app platform service into the manually launchable SDK app while keeping native picker ownership behind the ProGPU/Silk.NET service boundary.

Treat any recurrence of that screenshot shape as a stale fixed-version SDK smoke output/package cache first; run the SDK CI clean step or delete the `artifacts/bin`/`artifacts/obj` smoke outputs and `artifacts/nuget/ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchSmoke` before changing WPF layout, retained roots, or compositor coordinates.
- Advanced the ProGPU submodule to `8a8e965` (`Fix opacity mask review regressions`) for the remaining PR #17 review threads. Native opacity/geometry mask compilation now saves and restores both opacity and blend stacks while compiling mask textures under `SrcOver`, so destructive active blend modes affect masked content rather than clearing the mask. `DrawingContext.Append(..., translation)` now translates `PushOpacityMask` bounds along with other Rect-backed commands. Replied to and resolved both review threads, and validated with focused `AppendTranslatesOpacityMaskBounds` and `OpacityMaskCompilationDoesNotInheritActiveBlendMode` tests; the broader compositor review class still aborts in an existing WebGPU destroyed-texture test-host crash after 27 passing tests.

Rebuilt the SDK transport packages and verified SDK switch runtime smoke, external no-source-change SDK smoke, MVP direct validation, MVP `Application.Run` validation, and the focused SDK graph guard all pass against the refreshed package feed.

The undo check intentionally applies the `TextBox` template first because WPF's `ChangeBlockUndoRecord` records undo units only once the text control owns a `TextView`.

- Advanced the ProGPU submodule to `220d8a1` (`Fix WPF shader and clip review regressions`) for the latest PR #17 review threads. `DrawingContext.Append(..., translation)` now composes append offsets into `PushGeometryClip` command transforms, including clips that already have a geometry transform, so appended retained branches keep clip and content coordinates aligned. `WpfShaderEffectParams` render-cache keys now include the primary texture and sampler texture generations, so resized/reallocated textures invalidate the WPF shader-effect draw-parameter cache instead of reusing stale source bindings. Focused ProGPU validation passed for the new append/cache regression tests plus `WpfShaderEffectRenderTests`; the broad ProGPU test project still aborts in an existing native WebGPU destroyed-texture host crash after 171 passing tests and remains a backend lifetime follow-up.
- Advanced the ProGPU submodule to `996a65b` (`Fix deferred texture cleanup lifetime`) to close the destroyed-texture backend follow-up exposed by the broader ProGPU test run. `WgpuContext.CleanupPendingResources()` now releases queued texture handles without calling `TextureDestroy(...)`, allowing any still-referenced bind groups/views to drain naturally instead of poisoning a later WebGPU submit after texture-handle reuse. `Compositor` also purges disposed mask textures from its mask texture pool and mask bind-group caches, rejects disposed or foreign-context mask textures before binding, and snapshots the mask pool during compositor disposal so texture disposal events cannot mutate the list under enumeration. Validation passed for the new focused destroyed-texture and mask-pool regressions, the full `CompositorReviewRegressionTests` class with 54 passed, and `ProGPU.Tests` with 423 passed when excluding the three external DXF fixture tests that fail on local `/Users/wieslawsoltes/Downloads` file permissions; the full unfiltered project no longer aborts natively and only reports those three access failures.

This closes the first third-party theme-variant coverage gap while keeping theme probing and resource dictionaries in managed Xceed/WPF code.
- Extended the Xceed Toolkit resource/theme lane through dynamic resource mutation on controls exported by the free `Extended.Wpf.Toolkit` 5.1.2 assembly. The SDK-switched sample now binds `WatermarkTextBox.Watermark` plus `RangeSlider` lower/higher range brushes to application resources, replaces those resources during direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation, verifies the managed dependency-property values update and restore, and records a status change so render invalidation must happen without resizing. This keeps package resource lookup and theme-style mutation in WPF/Xceed code while ProGPU supplies dispatcher wakeups and final rendering. The separate Material control family appears in a different local Xceed package, not in the free `Extended.Wpf.Toolkit` dependency used by this SDK sample, so it remains classified rather than papered over with a conflicting second Toolkit assembly.
- Extended the source-backed AvalonDock lane through `ILayoutUpdateStrategy` and generated layout-item metadata updates. The SDK-switched sample now binds `SourceDockManager.LayoutUpdateStrategy` to a normal view-model strategy, validates document and anchorable before/after insertion callbacks, places source-backed layout items through AvalonDock's public model API, and mutates source document/anchorable titles plus close policy after generated `LayoutDocument`/`LayoutAnchorable` wrappers exist. Direct, `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation include the new `AvalonDock layout update strategy and dynamic metadata` marker, keeping docking placement and layout-item synchronization in managed Xceed/WPF rather than ProGPU bridge code.
- Extended the same source-backed AvalonDock lane through title-template selectors and generated `LayoutItem` command surfaces. The SDK-switched sample now declares document and anchorable title `DataTemplate`s, selects them through a normal `DataTemplateSelector`, validates selector dispatch for source view models and generated layout models, verifies generated document/anchorable `LayoutItem` command properties, and executes the generated activate commands through AvalonDock's public command objects. Direct, `Application.Run`, and live validation include the new `AvalonDock title selectors and layout item commands` marker, keeping tab/title selection and command binding in managed AvalonDock/WPF while ProGPU/Silk.NET remains responsible for input delivery, repaint wakeups, and rendering.
- Extended the Xceed Toolkit lane through `WindowContainer` and `ChildWindow` lifecycle coverage. The SDK-switched sample now hosts a modal `ChildWindow` inside the Xceed `WindowContainer`, opens it from normal WPF `Button.Click`, focuses an inner `TextBox`, accepts it through an inner button by setting `DialogResult`, records `Closing`/`Closed` event counts, and validates open/closed state during direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET runs. The live marker now includes `Toolkit child window lifecycle`, keeping toolkit transient window state, focus, modal container behavior, and closing events in managed Xceed/WPF while ProGPU supplies host input, dispatcher wakeups, invalidation, and rendering.
- Extended the same Xceed `WindowContainer` lane through embedded Toolkit `MessageBox` coverage. The sample now declares `xctk:MessageBox`, opens it with the instance `ShowMessageBox(...)` API instead of a native OS dialog, validates caption/text/default OK button/result/visibility state, closes it through the generated `PART_OkButton` routed click path during direct and bounded `Application.Run` validation, and drives the visible show button through live ProGPU/Silk.NET input before closing through WPF's generated template event route. The live marker now includes `Toolkit message box lifecycle`, keeping embedded Xceed message-box state in managed Toolkit/WPF while ProGPU owns host input, render wakeups, and final drawing.
- Extended the standalone Toolkit `MessageBox.Show(...)` lane through both owner forms exposed by the Xceed package. The SDK-switched sample now opens static message boxes with a WPF `Window` owner and with an `IntPtr` owner from `WindowInteropHelper.EnsureHandle()`, lets Xceed create its real transparent modal `Window`, closes it through generated `PART_OkButton`/`PART_NoButton` routed clicks inside the nested dispatcher frame, and validates balanced show/close counts plus the non-zero portable owner handle during bounded `Application.Run`. This keeps static Toolkit dialog construction, modal dispatch, owner-window setup, and button result policy in managed Xceed/WPF while ProGPU/Silk.NET supplies portable window activation, synthetic handles, and rendering.
- Extended the Xceed visual-interaction lane through `Zoombox` and `Magnifier`. The SDK-switched sample now hosts a `xctkz:Zoombox` with managed content, drives `Zoom(...)`, `ZoomTo(Rect)`, `FitToBounds()`, and `GoBack()` through normal routed button clicks, records `CurrentViewChanged` and `ViewStackIndexChanged` events, and attaches a resource-backed `Magnifier` with `MagnifierManager` so the adorner path is validated without placing the same magnifier in the layout tree. Direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation now include the `Toolkit zoombox and magnifier` marker over logical `980x640` / physical `1960x1280` Retina geometry, keeping viewport, scale, view-stack, and magnifier freeze/unfreeze behavior in managed Xceed/WPF while ProGPU supplies input, invalidation wakeups, and rendering.
- Added the first Xceed panel coverage with the free package's exposed `WrapPanel`. The Toolkit sample now validates `ItemWidth`, `ItemHeight`, orientation, child order, child count, loaded layout participation, and the live `Toolkit panels` marker. Other documented panel classes such as `Canvas`, `RadialCanvas`, and `AutoStretchStackPanel` appear in the package XML metadata/resources but are not XAML-creatable public types in the current free package build, so they remain classified separately instead of being papered over with ProGPU-side shims.
- Extended the Xceed collection-editor lane through `CollectionControl`. The SDK-switched sample now binds `ItemsSource`, `ItemsSourceType`, `NewItemTypes`, and two-way `SelectedItem` to a normal WPF view model, validates labels/read-only state and the embedded `PropertyGrid`, mutates the observable collection through visible sample buttons, selects an existing item, and runs the same direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation. This keeps collection editor state, new-item type metadata, selection, and property-grid composition in managed Xceed/WPF while ProGPU supplies host input, layout, invalidation wakeups, and rendering.
- Extended the same collection-editor lane through `CollectionControlButton` and `CollectionControlDialog` creation. The SDK-switched sample now binds the package button to the same collection source/type/new-item metadata, handles the routed `CollectionUpdated` event, constructs the public dialog with the same managed bindings, and drives the real button click during bounded `Application.Run` validation while a dispatcher timer observes and closes the modal dialog. Live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation now includes the `Toolkit collection control and dialog button` marker; deeper dialog-template sizing remains separate fidelity work instead of being worked around in app code.
- Extended the source-backed AvalonDock lane through generated document tab-group commands. The SDK-switched sample now exposes a visible `Tab group commands` button, ensures a second source-backed document, executes the generated `NewHorizontalTabGroupCommand` and `NewVerticalTabGroupCommand`, validates the created sibling `LayoutDocumentPaneGroup` orientation/child movement, then executes `MoveToPreviousTabGroupCommand` to restore the source document pane. Direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation now include the `AvalonDock tab group commands` marker, keeping document tab grouping in managed AvalonDock/WPF while ProGPU supplies host input, dispatcher wakeups, invalidation, and rendering.
- Extended the Xceed window primitive lane through direct `WindowControl` coverage. The SDK-switched sample now hosts a visible `xctk:WindowControl` inside its own `WindowContainer`, validates caption/icon/style/border/template parts, binds inner text state, routes `Activated`, `HeaderMouseLeftButtonClicked`, `HeaderDragDelta`, and `CloseButtonClicked`, and drives focus/text input plus the generated `PART_CloseButton` through live ProGPU/Silk.NET input. Direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live validation now include the `Toolkit window control primitive` marker, keeping Toolkit window chrome/template/routed-event behavior in managed Xceed/WPF instead of adding ProGPU bridge shims.
- Expanded the Xceed `WindowControl` primitive lane through the package-selected asset's header/icon routed events. The SDK-switched sample now routes `HeaderIconClicked`, `HeaderIconDoubleClicked`, `HeaderMouseLeftButtonDoubleClicked`, and `HeaderMouseRightButtonClicked` through `AddHandler(...)`, then exercises those events during direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation. This keeps Toolkit window gesture policy in managed Xceed/WPF while the SDK supplies host input, repaint wakeups, and rendering. The separate Xceed package XML documents additional `WindowControl` members such as `ResizeMode`, `TitleAlignment`, `MaximizeButtonClicked`, `MinimizeButtonClicked`, and `WindowResizeThumbDrag`, but the `Extended.Wpf.Toolkit` assembly selected by the SDK sample does not expose them, so those remain classified rather than worked around in app code.
- Extended the collection-editor dialog lane through accepted OK persistence. The SDK-switched sample now opens the real `CollectionControlButton` modal dialog during bounded `Application.Run` validation, uses the embedded `CollectionControl` command binding to add a default-constructed sample entry, edits that entry, clicks the dialog's default OK button, observes the routed `CollectionUpdated` event, and validates the bound source collection receives the new item and status update. This keeps dialog OK policy, command creation, modal dispatch, and source persistence in managed Xceed/WPF.
- Extended the collection-editor dialog lane through cancel rollback. The SDK-switched sample now opens the real `CollectionControlButton` modal dialog during bounded `Application.Run` validation, mutates an existing entry, creates and edits a new entry through the embedded `CollectionControl` command binding, clicks the dialog's Cancel button, verifies `CollectionUpdated` does not fire, and validates the bound source collection restores its original values while discarding the canceled entry. This keeps rollback policy, modal dispatch, and editor cloning behavior in managed Xceed/WPF.
- Extended AvalonDock through auto-hide overlay keyboard navigation in the SDK-switched Toolkit sample. The app now binds `F11` to a normal `RoutedUICommand`, locates AvalonDock's generated auto-hide anchor controls, invokes the real overlay show/hide methods, verifies the overlay model contains the expected anchorables, and validates the same command through live ProGPU/Silk.NET key input. This exposed and closed portable native-boundary gaps in `HwndHost`, `HwndSource`, `UnsafeNativeMethods.GetParent`, and the SDK's user32 compatibility shim (`GetCapture`/`SetCapture`/`ReleaseCapture`, `WindowFromPoint`, `ScreenToClient`, `ClientToScreen`, and cursor APIs). Verified focused Toolkit `Application.Run` and live apphost validation after repacking the managed WPF transport and SDK packages.
- Extended the AvalonDock anchorable lifecycle lane through `LayoutAnchorable.Hiding` and `IsVisibleChanged` event coverage. The SDK-switched Toolkit sample now subscribes to the property pane anchorable lifecycle events, records the affected content ID in the view model, validates hide/show membership in the hidden collection, and requires the same counters to advance during bounded `Application.Run` and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation. This keeps anchorable lifecycle policy in managed AvalonDock/WPF while ProGPU supplies input, render wakeups, and rendering.
- Extended the AvalonDock closable-anchorable lane through `LayoutAnchorable.Closing` and `Closed` event coverage. The SDK-switched Toolkit sample now marks the activity anchorable closable, drives close/reopen through normal WPF buttons, records closing/closed content IDs in the view model, verifies pane removal/reinsertion, and exercises the same path during direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation before the existing auto-hide checks. This keeps anchorable close policy and layout membership in managed AvalonDock/WPF.
- Fixed the Toolkit sample scroll-clipping regression in the WPF visual reflection layer instead of adding app-side workarounds. Real WPF stores ScrollViewer viewport clipping as protected `Visual.VisualScrollableAreaClip`, while the transition shim tests only exposed `ScrollableAreaClip`; `WpfVisualTreeRenderer` now reads and tracks both names, maps valid rectangles into immediate and retained ProGPU clip state, and rebases the clip correctly when cache/effect owners create bounded native layers. The Toolkit/AvalonDock sample now names its scroll viewport and content panel and validates a real non-zero scroll offset during direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation, resetting the offset before later input checks.
- Fixed the follow-up Toolkit scroll clipping gap where retained WPF visuals could keep using stale scroll placement until a resize or unrelated full invalidation forced replay. `WpfVisualInvalidationTracker` now snapshots low-level visual state that WPF mutates during scrolling and layout, including visual offset, `VisualScrollableAreaClip`/`ScrollableAreaClip`, clip/transform references, opacity, and render size, and marks the retained branch dirty when those values change without an event or version bump. Added focused tracker regressions for visual offset and scrollable-area clip changes, then validated the rebuilt SDK/package path through the full Toolkit apphost smoke.
- Extended the compile-visible `Extended.Wpf.Toolkit` `WindowControl` primitive surface through `WindowThickness`. The SDK-switched sample now sets the property in the same managed setup path used for header/icon event registration and validates the value during direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET coverage. This keeps the distinction between the package actually shipped in the SDK lane and the broader standalone Xceed package XML, where resize-thumb and max/minimize routed events remain unavailable in the selected assembly.
- Extended the compile-visible AvalonDock `DockingManager` option surface in the SDK-switched Toolkit sample. The primary and source-backed managers now declare normal XAML for mixed orientation and grid-splitter dimensions, while the primary manager also declares system-menu suppression and auto-hide close timing; direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation assert those dependency-property values from SDK-built BAML and include the `AvalonDock manager options` marker. `CacheDocumentTabItems` and `CanFloatBehindMainWindow` are present in the separate `Xceed.Wpf.AvalonDock` package XML but absent from the `Extended.Wpf.Toolkit` 5.1.2 assembly selected by this SDK sample, so they remain classified instead of being papered over by bridge code or a conflicting package.
- Extended the source-backed AvalonDock command lane through generated anchorable auto-hide and dock commands. The SDK-switched sample now executes `LayoutAnchorableItem.AutoHideCommand`, verifies the generated source-backed model moves into one of AvalonDock's side groups, then executes `DockCommand` and verifies normal pane membership is restored. This keeps source-backed anchorable command policy inside managed AvalonDock/WPF and gives the remaining auto-hide hover/timer work a stronger command-state baseline.
- Extended the external SDK no-source-change gate through a third-party package reference. `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkExternalSmokeHarness` now generates an app that references `Extended.Wpf.Toolkit` in its normal WPF project file before switching only the root SDK to `ProGPU.Wpf.Sdk`, compiles Xceed `WatermarkTextBox`/`IntegerUpDown` controls and a simple AvalonDock layout, validates Toolkit binding and AvalonDock manager/model state at runtime, and verifies Xceed Toolkit/AvalonDock assemblies plus deps are present in the SDK-produced output. The generated AvalonDock manager explicitly selects the package Aero theme, matching the repo-local Toolkit sample path and avoiding the default package template image URI path that still depends on WIC/COM on non-Windows.
- Added the first large tabular workload to the Toolkit/AvalonDock SDK sample. The new `DataGrid 100k` AvalonDock document hosts WPF's `DataGrid` with 100,000 generated rows, explicit row/column virtualization, recycling mode, pixel scrolling, selection binding, and first/last-row validation in direct, bounded, live apphost, and project-graph coverage. The selected free `Extended.Wpf.Toolkit` package does not contain `Xceed.Wpf.DataGrid`/`DataGridControl`, so this keeps a high-volume WPF Toolkit-era grid performance surface in the current Xceed/AvalonDock lane while leaving the separate commercial Xceed DataGrid package as a future compatibility branch.
- Extended the same `DataGrid 100k` lane through real large-offset scrolling and realized-row bounds. Loaded direct, bounded `Application.Run`, and live ProGPU/Silk.NET validation now activates the AvalonDock DataGrid document, resolves the template `ScrollViewer`, scrolls to the last generated row with `DataGrid.ScrollIntoView(...)`, verifies a non-zero vertical offset, asserts realized `DataGridRow` visuals remain bounded under virtualization, then resets back to the first row for manual evaluation. This ties the 100k grid sample to the same scrolling/clipping/invalidation surface that exposed earlier Toolkit regressions.
- Extended the external SDK no-source-change gate with the same class of large tabular workload. `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkExternalSmokeHarness` now generates a default-item SDK app containing a 100,000-row WPF `DataGrid`, explicit row/column virtualization, recycling mode, pixel scrolling, two-way selection binding, large-offset `ScrollIntoView(...)` validation, and realized-row bounds. This proves the custom SDK path can exercise high-volume WPF `DataGrid` behavior without app-side ProGPU APIs or repo-local project props.
- Expanded the external SDK no-source-change third-party package gate beyond the initial Xceed editor pair. The generated external app now compiles and validates Xceed `ColorPicker`, `CalculatorUpDown`, `DropDownButton`, and `SplitButton` from the normal `Extended.Wpf.Toolkit` package, including binding source updates, loaded popup open/close state, dropdown content rooted through the portable public `HwndSource` facade, and routed button actions that close the popups. This lifts a stable subset of the repo-local Toolkit popup coverage into the outside-repo SDK migration contract.
- Corrected the Toolkit/AvalonDock scroll clipping model after visual inspection showed the left Toolkit panel and the 100k-row `DataGrid` bleeding outside their viewports. ProGPU now exposes an `OuterClipBounds` visual state and applies it through the parent transform, while `WpfVisualTreeRenderer` maps WPF `VisualScrollableAreaClip` there instead of merging it into local `ClipBounds`; normal WPF `Clip` remains local-space. The immediate fallback path temporarily removes and restores the visual-local transform around scrollable-area clip pushes, and opacity-mask/effect/cache bounds inference now intersects scrollable clips after child transform/offset projection. Added ProGPU pixel and invalidation regressions plus WPF retained/fallback bridge regressions, then validated the rebuilt SDK path with external SDK smoke, Hello/MVP live probes, focused graph guard, Toolkit direct apphost validation, and Toolkit live validation over `980x640` logical / `1960x1280` physical geometry.
- Advanced the ProGPU submodule for the latest PR #17 ShaderToy hex-literal review. `ShaderToyTranspiler` now parses overflowing unsuffixed hexadecimal integer literals such as `0xffffffff` as `uint` when they exceed `int.MaxValue`, so WPF-facing shader sources remain on the native WGSL path instead of producing invalid negative `u32` literals or requiring managed source rewrites. Verified the ProGPU test build and focused ShaderToy regression slice with the new overflowing-hex test.
- Advanced the ProGPU submodule again for the latest PR #17 ACIS static-buffer review. Static DXF compilation now preserves `DrawAcisSolid(..., modelTransform)` records by passing the command model transform into the ACIS extension compile path for both provider-backed drawing contexts and provider-less command lists, while the dynamic visual path still consumes the already-composed parent/model transform once. Verified the ProGPU test build plus focused ACIS static-record, dynamic-transform, and ShaderToy overflowing-hex regressions.
- Fixed the remaining Toolkit/AvalonDock visual clipping bleed by lowering rectangular WPF visual clips and `ScrollableAreaClip`/`VisualScrollableAreaClip` scopes to ProGPU native `PushClip(Rect)` commands with the active WPF transform instead of forcing them through geometry mask paths. Rounded or non-rectangular clips still use native geometry clips. This keeps scroll viewer and DataGrid viewport clipping in WPF logical DIPs while ProGPU owns scissor/pixel conversion, and it avoids app-side Toolkit or DataGrid workarounds. Added command-sink and visual-tree regressions, then rebuilt the mutable SDK packages and validated external SDK smoke, Hello/MVP live probes, focused graph guard, and Toolkit live validation over `980x640` logical / `1960x1280` physical geometry.
- Expanded the external no-source-change SDK gate with additional third-party Xceed controls. The generated external app now compiles and validates Xceed `BusyIndicator` and `PropertyGrid` from a normal `Extended.Wpf.Toolkit` `PackageReference`, including busy-state two-way binding and selected-object binding, alongside the existing Toolkit editor, popup, AvalonDock, and 100k DataGrid coverage.
- Extended the same native rectangle clip policy into decoded WPF MIL render data. `WpfMilRenderDataDecoder` now lowers plain `RectangleGeometry` and exact axis-aligned rectangle path `MilPushClip` records to ProGPU native `PushClip(Rect)` commands with the active transform, while non-rectangular render-data clips stay on the geometry-mask path. Verified the bridge and test builds plus focused decoder clip coverage for rectangle, transformed arc, complex transformed arc, and non-rectangular path clips.
- Advanced the ProGPU submodule to `3d080f2` for the latest PR #17 review pass. `SKRect.Union(...)` now treats the current or incoming empty rectangle as an empty bounds accumulator instead of pinning unions to the origin, and `ShaderToyTranspiler` now accepts positive integer constant expressions, including scoped `const int`/`const uint` identifiers, as GLSL array sizes. Verified with ProGPU restore, serial `ProGPU.Tests` build, and focused review-regression coverage for `SKRect` union plus neighboring ShaderToy constant/hex/shift tests.
- Fixed the remaining Toolkit/AvalonDock viewport clipping gap shown in the left Toolkit panel and 100k-row WPF `DataGrid`. WPF materializes layout clips through protected `Visual.VisualClip` after `UIElement.ensureClip(...)`, while the public `UIElement.Clip` dependency property can remain null; the reflection renderer now reads `VisualClip` first, falls back to `Clip` for shim/pre-layout objects, registers `VisualClip` as retained dependency state, and the retained invalidation tracker snapshots the same internal clip so layout-only viewport changes trigger replay without a resize. Added retained visual-state and tracker regressions for internal visual clips, rebuilt `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests`, and validated direct plus live Toolkit apphost paths over `980x640` logical / `1960x1280` physical geometry.
- Tightened the Toolkit/AvalonDock sample validation so this class of clipping regression is caught in the sample itself. The left Toolkit pane and 100k-row WPF `DataGrid` validation now resolves the loaded `ScrollContentPresenter` under each `ScrollViewer` and asserts that WPF produced a finite internal `VisualClip` rectangle before exercising large-offset scrolling. Revalidated direct and live Toolkit apphost paths.
- Stabilized the WPF bridge verification slice after the clipping work. Contextless, pointerless fake `GpuTexture` instances are now accepted by `WpfBitmapSourceImageAdapter` only as command-recording test doubles, while ProGPU's compositor null-guards texture context checks and still requires an owned context plus non-null texture/view pointers before binding. The bridge tests now assert WPF dash arrays stay in thickness-relative units and that render wakeups flush queued input before painting, matching the existing ProGPU-native dash and input/render invalidation contracts. Verified `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` at 686/686, `ProGPU.Tests` with the local-file DXF diagnostics filtered at 456/456, and `ProGPU.Tests.Headless` with the local-file Markdown diagnostic filtered at 102/102.
- Extended the external no-source-change SDK default-item gate through cursor resource discovery. The generated default-item WPF app now places `Assets/DefaultItemsCursor.cur` under normal SDK item discovery, binds it through XAML `FrameworkElement.Cursor`, and loads the same pack resource through `Application.GetResourceStream(...)` plus `new Cursor(stream)`. This keeps cursor asset lookup, BAML URI resolution, and WPF cursor object construction in the managed WPF/SDK layer while leaving native cursor decoding and platform cursor presentation as ProGPU/Silk.NET service work.
- Forwarded managed WPF cursor requests from `PortablePresentationSource` into the ProGPU/Silk.NET cursor service. `IMouseInputProvider.SetCursor(...)` now records the requested WPF cursor, raises a portable cursor event, and the host bridge maps common WPF cursor names to `WpfCursor` values before applying them through `SilkNetWpfCursorService`, keeping `QueryCursor` and control cursor policy in WPF instead of app-side ProGPU code.
- Tightened the remaining Toolkit/AvalonDock clipping gap shown in the left Toolkit panel and 100k-row WPF `DataGrid`. Some WPF controls compute viewport clips through `GetLayoutClipInternal()` before or without exposing a populated public `Clip`; the reflection renderer now probes that protected layout clip after `VisualClip` and intersects it with an explicit user clip as a native rectangle when possible. Added retained and immediate replay regressions for layout-only clips and layout-plus-explicit clip intersections, keeping ScrollViewer/DataGrid viewport clipping on WPF layout state and ProGPU native scissor conversion. Revalidated the Toolkit direct apphost path and live ProGPU/Silk.NET path over `980x640` logical / `1960x1280` physical geometry, including the `Toolkit DataGrid 100k virtualization` marker.
- Added the first ProGPU-owned DirectX compatibility core for SciChart-class WPF charting work. The ProGPU submodule now contains a reusable `ProGPU.DirectX` project with feature-level negotiation for Direct3D9_3/10_0/10_1/11_0/11_1, resource formats/usages, GPU-backed or metadata-mode devices, 2D textures, render-target swap-chain back buffers, vertex/index/constant buffers, immediate command recording, viewport/scissor/topology state, clear/draw/draw-indexed/present command capture, GPU-backed clear submission through the owning `WgpuContext`, native backend handle probing, and strong-name coverage.
