This is the durable backend boundary for DirectX-shaped chart/rendering integrations; vendor-specific SciChart adapter/binary-shim work still needs the actual SciChart DirectX interop surface.
- Wired the DirectX compatibility core into the WPF SDK deliverable. `ProGPU.Wpf` now references `ProGPU.DirectX` and exposes a host-owned `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.DirectXDevice` bound to the active Silk.NET/WebGPU `WgpuContext`; `ProGPU.Wpf.Sdk` carries `ProGPU.DirectX` in package-reference, local-artifact, mutable-output clearing, SDK-switch runtime, external SDK smoke, and SDK CI package creation paths. Focused validation covered the new ProGPU DirectX tests, strong-name signing, `ProGPU.Wpf` build, and the WPF managed project graph guard.
- Addressed two outstanding ProGPU PR review items while the branch was open for the DirectX work. WinUI `PathGeometry.Parse(...)` now copies the parsed vector fill rule into the WinUI shim result, and `ShaderToyExtensionPipeline` includes a stable shader-source hash in shader/pipeline cache keys so same logical shader keys with different source text cannot alias native shader modules or render pipelines. Focused ProGPU validation covered the path fill-rule test and new ShaderToy source-key regression.
- Extended `ProGPU.DirectX` beyond resources and command metadata with Direct3D-shaped shader, input-layout, graphics-pipeline, compute-pipeline, blend, depth/stencil, and rasterizer descriptors. WGSL shaders now compile to WebGPU shader modules when a `WgpuContext` is available, graphics/compute pipelines can create native WebGPU pipeline handles for GPU-backed devices, HLSL text and bytecode are preserved as metadata for the forthcoming translator or SharpDX/COM facade, and the immediate context records shader, input-layout, pipeline, fixed-state, draw-indexed, and dispatch bindings. Focused tests now cover a SciChart-style POSITION/COLOR indexed 3D pipeline, HLSL-bytecode metadata, wrong-stage rejection, compute dispatch metadata, and strong-name coverage.
- Extended the same DirectX shim through shader-resource views, unordered-access views, sampler states, stage/slot binding state, and texture/buffer copy command recording. GPU-backed texture views and samplers can now expose WebGPU handles, metadata-mode preserves buffer and HLSL-era binding descriptors for future SciChart/SharpDX mapping, and immediate contexts track SRV/sampler/UAV slots separately from draw/dispatch commands. Focused tests cover texture and structured-buffer SRV binding, sampler normalization, UAV binding, copy-resource commands, and invalid usage rejection.
- Extended `ProGPU.DirectX` through Direct3D-style binding snapshots. Immediate contexts now track constant buffers by shader stage and slot, validate constant-buffer usage, snapshot live constant-buffer/SRV/sampler/UAV state onto draw, draw-indexed, dispatch, and explicit apply-bindings commands, and dispose command-owned native binding resources through the existing `WgpuContext` deferred cleanup path. GPU-backed snapshots opportunistically create WebGPU bind groups for constant buffers, texture and buffer SRVs, samplers, and buffer UAVs when native handles are available; texture UAVs and geometry-stage bindings remain explicit metadata until the storage-texture and geometry-facade execution path is designed. Focused validation covers graphics VS/PS binding snapshots, compute SRV/UAV snapshots, invalid constant-buffer usage, DirectX shim tests, and strong-name coverage.
- Extended `ProGPU.DirectX` through the first native execution path for supported Direct3D-shaped commands. GPU-backed immediate contexts now snapshot render targets, depth targets, viewport/scissor state, vertex/index buffers, index format, pipelines, and binding snapshots onto draw commands, submit compatible clear, copy-buffer, draw, draw-indexed, and compute dispatch commands through WebGPU encoders, and expose submission counters for diagnostics. Draw/dispatch flushes fail closed when backend-compatible resources or bind groups are missing instead of silently falling back to managed behavior. Focused validation covers deferred vertex/index state capture, a GPU-backed WGSL triangle draw with readback, GPU-backed compute dispatch, DirectX shim tests, and strong-name coverage.
- Extended the DirectX execution path with basic 3D frame setup primitives needed by SciChart-class renderers. Texture `CopyResource` now stays in the flushed command stream instead of executing out-of-band, GPU-backed texture copies increment native copy diagnostics and destination texture generation through `GpuTexture.CopyFrom(...)`, `ClearDepthStencil(...)` accepts Direct3D-style depth/stencil clear flags and submits a depth-stencil render pass, and graphics-pipeline creation now initializes stencil front/back state explicitly so depth-enabled pipelines no longer rely on invalid zero-valued native enum defaults. Focused validation covers native texture-copy readback, depth-stencil clear followed by a depth-enabled draw, DirectX shim tests, and strong-name coverage.
- Extended the DirectX shim through CPU-readable staging/readback resources. `DxCpuAccessFlags` now marks buffers and textures as CPU-readable, `GpuBuffer.ReadBytes(...)` supports WebGPU `MapRead` staging buffers and copy-source readback through a temporary readback buffer, DirectX buffers expose byte and typed reads with a CPU shadow fallback for metadata devices, and DirectX textures expose guarded `ReadPixels(...)` for GPU-backed copy-source textures. Focused validation covers metadata-mode shadow copies and GPU-backed staging-buffer copies.
- Extended DirectX texture UAV binding snapshots onto native WebGPU storage textures. GPU-backed unordered-access texture views now satisfy backend bind-group creation, lower to write-only `StorageTextureBindingLayout` entries, and bind their native texture view in compute snapshots while buffer UAV behavior remains unchanged. Focused validation covers a GPU-backed texture UAV bind-group snapshot.
- Extended GPU buffer readback to support unaligned byte-range reads needed by Direct3D staging-style inspection. `GpuBuffer.ReadBytes(...)` now maps or copies an aligned enclosing range and slices the requested bytes, so `ProGPU.DirectX` CPU-readable buffers and backend copy-source buffers no longer require caller 4-byte-aligned offsets and lengths for ordinary staging reads. Focused validation covers unaligned byte reads through both MapRead staging buffers and copy-source readback.
- Extended DirectX texture execution with native color MSAA resolve commands. `ResolveResource(...)` and `ResolveSubresource(...)` now record Direct3D-shaped resolve metadata, validate sample-count, format, usage, and subresource constraints, execute WebGPU render-pass resolves from multisampled render targets into single-sample render targets, mark destination texture generations, and expose `SubmittedResolveCount` diagnostics. Focused validation covers metadata capture and a GPU-backed 4x MSAA clear resolved into a readable texture.
- Added focused validation for native DirectX line primitive execution. GPU-backed `LineList` pipelines now have a readback regression that clears a target, draws a WGSL line primitive through the DirectX immediate context, and verifies submitted draw diagnostics plus rendered pixels, so SciChart-style chart lines no longer depend on untested rasterizer behavior. Triangle-wireframe emulation remains separate because WebGPU has no direct polygon fill-mode state.
- Added cached triangle-wireframe edge expansion for GPU-backed DirectX pipelines. `DxFillMode.Wireframe` triangle-list and triangle-strip pipelines now lower to WebGPU line-list pipelines, immediate-context draws build or reuse edge index buffers keyed by draw range and source index-buffer generation, DirectX buffers keep upload shadows for indexed expansion without GPU readback stalls, and `SubmittedWireframeDrawCount` exposes diagnostics. Focused validation covers non-indexed and UInt16 indexed wireframe triangle draws with readback.
- Extended DirectX depth/stencil state through Direct3D-style front/back stencil operations. `DxDepthStencilStateDescriptor` now carries read/write masks, stencil reference, and independent front/back compare/fail/depth-fail/pass operations; GPU-backed pipelines map those operations to WebGPU stencil state, stencil-only passes keep depth writes disabled, draws set the stencil reference on the render pass, and invalid stencil formats fail during pipeline creation. Focused validation covers metadata capture, invalid descriptor rejection, and a GPU-backed replace/equal stencil flow with readback.
- Extended DirectX buffers through Direct3D-style map/unmap semantics for dynamic and staging data. `DxMapMode` now covers read, write, read/write, write-discard, and write-no-overwrite flows; immediate contexts expose `Map(...)`/`Unmap(...)`; buffers validate CPU access, reject nested mappings, synchronize readable GPU-backed ranges into the mapping span, and upload mapped write ranges back to the native WebGPU buffer on unmap. Focused validation covers metadata read/write maps, partial no-overwrite writes, invalid access/range rejection, and GPU-backed mapped uploads with native readback.
- Extended DirectX texture mapping for the color Texture2D path used by dynamic chart resources. `ProGpuDirectXMappedSubresource` now represents either a buffer or texture, immediate contexts can map/unmap Texture2D subresource 0, mapped texture ranges expose Direct3D row/depth pitches, metadata devices keep CPU pixel shadows, GPU-backed readable maps synchronize through native texture readback, and mapped write-discard/no-overwrite flows upload back through WebGPU texture writes on unmap. The supported path is intentionally single-sample, single-mip, single-array color textures in formats already covered by backend upload/readback; depth/stencil, arrays, mips, multisample, and wider vector formats remain explicit backend work. Focused validation covers metadata read/write maps, invalid access and unsupported subresource rejection, and GPU-backed mapped texture upload with native readback.
- Extended DirectX texture UAV binding snapshots with explicit storage texture access metadata. `DxUnorderedAccessViewDescriptor` now distinguishes write-only, read-only, and read/write access, texture bind-group layouts lower that access to WebGPU storage-texture access when supported, and the backend fails closed for read-only/read-write texture UAV bind groups unless `PROGPU_ENABLE_READWRITE_STORAGE_TEXTURES=1` opts into a runtime known to support it. The current wgpu-native `wgpuInstanceHasWGSLLanguageFeature` entry point aborts in this dependency set, so automatic capability probing remains open rather than risking process termination. Focused validation covers access metadata preservation, invalid access rejection, write-only GPU texture UAV bind groups, and guarded read/write texture UAV snapshots.
- Extended the DirectX shader path with a constrained HLSL text translator for native WebGPU execution. `ProGPU.DirectX` now translates simple semantic-declared HLSL vertex/pixel/compute entry points into WGSL, exposes the generated backend source for diagnostics, and uses the translated source to create GPU-backed shader modules and pipelines when the source fits the supported subset. HLSL bytecode and broader language/resource features remain metadata-only until a full compiler/import path or SharpDX/Direct3D facade is wired in. Focused validation covers unsupported HLSL metadata preservation and a GPU-backed HLSL text vertex/pixel triangle draw with native readback.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL path through MVP-style uniform transforms needed by SciChart-class chart shaders. The translator now lowers `cbuffer ... : register(b#)` blocks into WGSL uniform structs, maps `float4x4` to native matrices, translates simple HLSL `mul(matrix, vector)` expressions, and qualifies constant-buffer field references. GPU-backed draw and dispatch execution now keeps command snapshots as state captures and creates transient bind groups from `RenderPipelineGetBindGroupLayout(...)` and `ComputePipelineGetBindGroupLayout(...)`, fixing WebGPU validation for implicit shader layouts and uniform `min_binding_size` requirements without allocating an unused explicit layout per draw. Focused validation covers a GPU-backed HLSL transform vertex shader with a real constant buffer, native draw submission, and rendered-pixel readback.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL path through the first native texture/sampler resource subset needed by SciChart-class chart shaders. `Texture2D` and `SamplerState` declarations with `register(t#)`/`register(s#)` now lower to native WGSL `texture_2d<f32>` and `sampler` bindings, simple `Texture2D.Sample(SamplerState, uv)` calls translate to `textureSample(...)`, and a deterministic stage/kind/register binding map lets vertex constant buffers and pixel shader resources coexist without compact-binding drift. GPU-only `Texture2D.WritePixels(...)` uploads now skip absent CPU shadows instead of requiring CPU access just to seed shader resources. Focused validation covers a GPU-backed HLSL vertex transform plus pixel texture sample draw with real SRV/sampler bindings and rendered-pixel readback.
- Extended the same DirectX HLSL texture path through initialized local variables, sample calls inside larger expressions, and explicit LOD sampling. The translator now rewrites `float4 sampled = Texture2D.Sample(...)` style locals, nested `Texture2D.Sample(...)` calls, and `Texture2D.SampleLevel(...)` to WGSL without requiring managed shader-source rewrites, while preserving constructor arguments with commas. Focused validation covers translation of initialized sampled locals plus nested `Sample(...)`/`SampleLevel(...)` expressions and a GPU-backed `SampleLevel(...)` local variable multiplied by a tint with rendered readback.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL path with broader intrinsic lowering needed by chart/effect and 3D lighting shader code. Common scalar/vector math and lighting helpers now translate inside ordinary expressions and initialized locals, including `abs`, trigonometry, `min`/`max`, `clamp`, `dot`, `cross`, `normalize`, `length`, `distance`, `reflect`, `refract`, `pow`, `sqrt`, `rsqrt`, `rcp`, `mad`, `saturate`, `lerp`, `frac`, `smoothstep`, and pixel derivatives `ddx`/`ddy`. This lets SciChart-class shaders keep more DirectX-style source instead of relying on WPF-side managed source rewrites. Focused validation covers nested intrinsic translation inside `Texture2D.Sample(...)`/`SampleLevel(...)` expressions plus a GPU-backed sampled draw using normalized-lighting math.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL matrix path for 3D chart shaders. `mul(...)` now lowers through the same recursive function-call translator as other intrinsics, so both `mul(matrix, vector)` and `mul(vector, matrix)` forms work, including nested expressions such as normal-vector transforms. The type mapper now covers `float2x2` through `float4x4` matrix declarations and constructors instead of only `float4x4`. Focused validation covers `float3x3` normal-matrix translation and a GPU-backed vector-first `mul(float4(position, 1), WorldViewProjection)` draw with readback.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL texture path with exact texel fetch support. `Texture2D.Load(int3(location), optional int2 offset)` now lowers to WGSL `textureLoad(...)`, validates that the source is a declared `Texture2D`, preserves the HLSL mip component as the load level, and folds the optional texel offset into native integer coordinates. Focused validation covers nested `Load(...)` translation beside `Sample(...)`/`SampleLevel(...)` and a GPU-backed pixel shader that combines sampler and texel-load reads against the same SRV.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL texture path with explicit LOD bias and gradient sampling. `Texture2D.SampleBias(SamplerState, uv, bias)` and `Texture2D.SampleGrad(SamplerState, uv, ddx, ddy)` now lower to WGSL `textureSampleBias(...)` and `textureSampleGrad(...)`, validate declared texture/sampler resources, and stay inside native WebGPU shader execution instead of requiring managed shader rewrites. Focused validation covers nested `Sample(...)`/`SampleLevel(...)`/`Load(...)`/`SampleBias(...)`/`SampleGrad(...)` translation plus a GPU-backed sampled draw with real SRV/sampler bindings and rendered readback.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL buffer-resource path with read-only typed `StructuredBuffer<T>` SRVs. `StructuredBuffer<float|floatN|floatMxN|intN|uintN> Name : register(t#)` now lowers to a native WGSL `var<storage, read>` runtime array at the same deterministic SRV binding, so chart vertex shaders can fetch point/position data by `SV_VertexID` through the ProGPU/WebGPU storage-buffer path instead of requiring managed vertex-buffer rewrites. Focused validation covers metadata translation of `StructuredBuffer<float4>` plus a GPU-backed draw that binds a DirectX buffer SRV and renders positions fetched from that structured buffer.
- Extended the same DirectX HLSL structured-buffer path through custom element records. Plain HLSL structs without semantics now lower to WGSL structs, semantic-bearing entry-point structs still get builtin/location attributes, and `StructuredBuffer<ChartPoint>` style resources bind as native read-only storage-buffer arrays with field access preserved in shader expressions. Focused validation covers translation of a `ChartPoint` record with position/color fields plus a GPU-backed draw that renders records fetched from a DirectX buffer SRV.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL compute path with writable structured-buffer UAVs. Compute-stage `RWStructuredBuffer<T> Name : register(u#)` now lowers to native WGSL `var<storage, read_write>` runtime arrays at deterministic DirectX UAV bindings, and indexed element/field assignments survive expression translation for native WebGPU dispatch. Focused validation covers metadata translation plus a GPU-backed dispatch that writes a `float4` through a DirectX buffer UAV and reads it back from the backend buffer.
- Extended the same DirectX HLSL buffer-resource path through typed `Buffer<T>` and compute `RWBuffer<T>` resources. `Buffer<float|floatN|floatMxN|intN|uintN>` SRVs now lower to native read-only storage-buffer arrays, and compute-stage `RWBuffer<T> register(u#)` lowers to native read/write storage-buffer UAV arrays, sharing the deterministic DirectX binding map with structured buffers. Focused validation covers metadata translation plus GPU-backed typed-buffer vertex fetch and RWBuffer dispatch/readback.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL raw-buffer path through `ByteAddressBuffer` and compute `RWByteAddressBuffer` resources. `ByteAddressBuffer register(t#)` now lowers to native read-only `array<u32>` SRV storage buffers, compute-stage `RWByteAddressBuffer register(u#)` lowers to native read/write `array<atomic<u32>>` UAV storage buffers, `Load`/`Load2`/`Load3`/`Load4` translate byte offsets to u32 storage-buffer element reads with `atomicLoad(...)` for writable buffers, `Store`/`Store2`/`Store3`/`Store4` emit `atomicStore(...)`, and `InterlockedAdd`/`InterlockedAnd`/`InterlockedOr`/`InterlockedXor`/`InterlockedMin`/`InterlockedMax`/`InterlockedExchange`/`InterlockedCompareExchange` lower to native WGSL atomics with optional original-value capture. Focused validation covers metadata translation plus GPU-backed dispatches that read raw input words, write summed values, and execute RWByteAddressBuffer interlocked add/or/xor readback. Compare-exchange execution is exposed through a backend capability and GPU pipeline creation is disabled on current Metal/WebGPU because that backend reports `MSL: FeatureNotImplemented("atomic CompareExchange")`.
- Extended DirectX instancing support for chart/marker batching. Immediate contexts now expose Direct3D-shaped `DrawInstanced(...)` and `DrawIndexedInstanced(...)` entry points over the existing command model, per-instance input-layout slots lower to native WebGPU instance-step vertex buffers, and HLSL-translated vertex shaders can consume per-instance attributes in a single draw. Focused validation covers metadata argument preservation plus a GPU-backed HLSL instanced draw that renders two colored instances from separate per-vertex and per-instance buffers with readback.
- Extended DirectX HLSL input-struct system-value handling for shader-library style chart batching. Semantic-bearing input fields now map `SV_VertexID` and `SV_InstanceID` to WGSL `vertex_index` and `instance_index` builtins, dispatch system values map to their WGSL builtins, and unsupported `SV_*` struct fields fail closed instead of silently consuming user locations. Focused validation covers metadata translation plus a GPU-backed HLSL `DrawInstanced(3, 2)` path that fetches triangle positions, instance offsets, and instance colors from structured-buffer SRVs without any managed vertex-buffer rewrite.
- Extended DirectX fragment system-value translation for 3D chart/material shaders. HLSL `bool` now maps through the translator, fragment `SV_IsFrontFace` lowers to WGSL `front_facing`, and pixel-output `SV_Depth` lowers to WGSL `frag_depth`. GPU-backed `SV_Depth` output is now validated through a native D32 depth-enabled draw/readback, while graphics pipelines that use `front_facing` remain capability-gated because the current backend accepts the WGSL but renders black; this keeps SciChart-style material shaders fail-closed until backend execution is proven instead of presenting a blank chart surface as a successful draw.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL pixel-shader path with `clip(...)` lowering for SciChart-class marker/surface/cutout shaders. Pixel-stage `clip(value)` now emits a WGSL discard guard, while vertex/compute use fails closed during translation. Focused validation covers metadata translation, rejection outside pixel shaders, and a GPU-backed HLSL draw that clears a target, runs a clipped pixel shader, and verifies discarded fragments leave the clear color intact.
- Extended the DirectX HLSL expression path with native conditional lowering for SciChart-class palette, threshold, and material shaders. Top-level HLSL `condition ? trueValue : falseValue` expressions now translate recursively to WGSL `select(falseValue, trueValue, condition)`, preserving texture/buffer/intrinsic/cbuffer expression rewriting inside each arm and keeping branchless shader decisions in ProGPU instead of managed source preprocessing. Focused validation covers metadata translation plus a GPU-backed HLSL pixel draw that chooses the true arm and verifies the rendered target through native readback.
- Added a reusable `ProGPU.DirectX` shader-bytecode reflection surface for compiled DirectX shader blobs. `ProGpuDirectXShader.BytecodeInfo` now classifies DXBC containers, raw DXIL headers, and raw DXIL bitcode; parses DXBC chunk tables; extracts tokenized shader program kind/model from `SHDR`/`SHEX`/`DXIL`; reflects `ISGN`/`ISG1`, `OSGN`/`OSG5`, and `PCSG` signature parameters; and reflects `RDEF` shader resource bindings. HLSL bytecode still does not create a native shader module until a real bytecode import/compiler path is connected, so existing compiled blobs are inspectable and routable while execution remains fail-closed. Focused validation covers malformed metadata-only DXBC bytecode plus a synthetic valid DXBC container with input signature, resource definition, and shader-model metadata.
- Extended compiled DirectX shader reflection into input-layout inference. `ProGpuDirectXShaderBytecodeInfo.TryCreateInputLayoutDescriptor(...)` now maps reflected non-system `ISGN` parameters into packed `DxInputElementDescriptor` entries with stable shader locations, configurable input slot/class/step rate, float/uint/sint scalar and vector formats, and fail-closed handling for unsupported component masks. This lets future SciChart/SharpDX adapters derive a native ProGPU input layout from shader bytecode metadata without managed WPF vertex declaration rewrites. Focused validation covers float position/color layouts, per-instance integer vector layouts, skipped system-value inputs, and unsupported-mask rejection.
- Surfaced reflected DirectX input-layout inference on graphics pipelines. `ProGpuDirectXGraphicsPipeline.EffectiveInputLayout` now prefers an explicit descriptor layout and otherwise derives one from the vertex shader bytecode `ISGN` signature, exposes `UsesReflectedInputLayout` plus fail-closed support/failure metadata, keys native pipeline creation on the effective layout, and makes `SetGraphicsPipeline(...)` update context input-layout state from that same effective layout. This lets future SciChart/SharpDX adapters submit compiled-shader pipelines without duplicating bytecode input-signature parsing or manually synchronizing context state. Focused validation covers automatic reflected layout use, explicit layout override, unsupported-mask failure reporting, and context state after pipeline binding.
- Extended compiled DirectX shader reflection into resource-binding requirements. `ProGpuDirectXShaderBytecodeInfo.TryCreateBindingRequirements(...)` now maps reflected `RDEF` resource types to ProGPU binding kinds for constant buffers, texture/structured/byte-address SRVs, samplers, and typed/structured/byte-address UAVs, preserving the shader stage, Direct3D bind slot/count, raw reflection metadata, and the deterministic native binding number used by ProGPU's runtime bind-group map. Unknown resource types fail closed. Focused validation covers mixed pixel-stage cbuffer/SRV/sampler/UAV metadata and unknown binding-type rejection.
- Surfaced reflected DirectX resource requirements directly on shader and pipeline metadata. `ProGpuDirectXShader.ReflectedBindingRequirements` now exposes supported bytecode `RDEF` requirements with fail-closed failure metadata for malformed or unsupported blobs, and `ProGpuDirectXGraphicsPipeline`/`ProGpuDirectXComputePipeline` aggregate the shader requirements so SciChart/SharpDX adapters can preflight native resources against a compiled DirectX pipeline without re-parsing bytecode or duplicating ProGPU binding-slot arithmetic. Focused validation covers shader-level requirements, unsupported binding failure reporting, graphics vertex+pixel aggregation, and compute UAV aggregation.
- Added DirectX context binding preflight against reflected shader/pipeline requirements. `ProGpuDirectXDeviceContext.ValidateGraphicsPipelineBindings(...)` and `ValidateComputePipelineBindings(...)` now compare the current constant-buffer/SRV/sampler/UAV bindings against the backend-owned requirements list, include missing-resource diagnostics on recorded draw/dispatch commands, honor array binding counts, and throw early when `ProGpuDirectXDeviceOptions.EnableValidation` is enabled. This gives future SciChart/SharpDX adapters a native fail-closed resource-validation path instead of silent missing-resource draws or WPF-side shader-resource bookkeeping. Focused validation covers missing sampler diagnostics, validation-enabled draw rejection, command metadata, successful graphics preflight, and compute UAV array-count validation.
- Added the first SciChart-facing texture/render-context bridge in `ProGPU.DirectX`, modeled on the public Visual Xccelerator `IRenderContext2D`/`ITexture2D` members found in `SciChart.Drawing.dll`. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartRenderContext2D` now creates a native render target, creates `Bgra8`, `Float32`, `UInt32`, and `Int32` textures, accepts SciChart-style color/float/integer uploads, records `DrawTexture(...)` operations, and submits GPU-backed point/linear filtered textured quads with optional uniform aspect fitting. Focused validation covers metadata/resource creation, fail-closed integer texture sampling, and a GPU-backed texture draw/readback. This is a reusable ProGPU DirectX surface, not a WPF managed bitmap workaround.
- Extended that SciChart bridge with native batched texture-vertex drawing for the public Visual Xccelerator `IVxRenderContext.DrawTexture(XyColorTextureVertex[], ...)` shape. The neutral `ProGpuDirectXSciChartTextureVertex` descriptor matches the observed SciChart `float X/Y/U/V + uint ColorArgb` layout, supports optional axis swapping, ARGB vertex tinting, clipped draw submission, and point/linear texture filtering. Focused validation covers metadata recording, empty-clip no-op behavior, and GPU-backed scissor/readback where the clipped side renders vertex-tinted texture data and the clipped-out side remains clear.
- Extended the SciChart bridge with a native shaped-heatmap path for the public Visual Xccelerator `DrawShapedHeatmap(...)` shape. `DrawTextureVertices(...)` now follows SciChart's `startIndex`/`count` range semantics, and `DrawShapedHeatmap(...)` submits a ProGPU-owned shader path over `XyColorTextureVertex` geometry, a `Float32` height field, a `Bgra8` gradient texture, color-map min/max constants, point/linear filtering, and the active clip. On Metal/WebGPU, R32Float textures cannot be auto-bound as filterable sampled textures, so ProGPU mirrors SciChart float height uploads into a read-only GPU buffer and samples full-precision heights from that buffer in the native shader rather than doing managed per-pixel conversion. Focused validation covers range recording, invalid range/range-order/texture-format rejection, and GPU-backed clipped heatmap readback.
- Extended the SciChart bridge with native height-texture contour drawing for the public Visual Xccelerator `DrawHeightTextureContours(...)` shape. The ProGPU path keeps Float32 height uploads in the GPU buffer mirror, validates the Bgra8 contour-mask texture plus z-range/stroke/opacity inputs, submits a blend-enabled shader over the requested viewport and active clip, and records contour draw diagnostics. It also fixes the Float32 mirror ownership so Bgra8 `SetData(...)` no longer creates or writes height buffers; only `SetFloatData(...)` updates the buffer-backed height field. Focused validation covers metadata recording, invalid contour inputs, empty-clip no-op behavior, GPU-backed clipped contour readback, SciChart-focused tests, the DirectX/signing subset, and `ProGPU.Wpf` build.
- Extended the SciChart bridge with a pen-aware native line-batch path for the public Visual Xccelerator `DrawLinesBatch(XyColorVertex[], count, IPen2D, isStrips, isDigital, isDrawNanAsGaps, transform)` shape. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartColorVertex` mirrors the observed `float X/Y/Offset + uint ColorArgb` layout, `ProGpuDirectXSciChartPen2D` preserves default ARGB, stroke thickness, and antialiasing intent, and `DrawLinesBatch(...)` records the original point stream plus pen/strip/digital/NaN policy. One-pixel paths stay on native WebGPU line-list draws, while thick pens expand into clipped solid-color triangle geometry in ProGPU so WPF does not tessellate SciChart series. Focused validation covers metadata recording, invalid counts, empty clips, strip versus segment mode, digital stepping, NaN gap versus closed-line policy, pen validation, clipped GPU readback, and GPU-backed thick-line readback. Deeper `Offset`/`IPen2D` semantics remain backend follow-up work.
- Extended the SciChart bridge with a native column-batch path for the public Visual Xccelerator `DrawColumnsBatch(XyColumnVertex[], ...)` shape. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartColumnVertex` mirrors the observed `float X/Y/Width/Height + uint FillColorArgb/StrokeColorArgb` layout, `DrawColumnsBatch(...)` records the source column stream, honors axis swapping and empty clips, skips non-finite or transparent columns, submits fill rectangles as native colored triangles, and submits one-pixel outlines as native line-list segments through the shared solid-color pipeline. Focused validation covers metadata recording, invalid counts, empty clips, fill/stroke vertex counts, clipped GPU readback, SciChart-focused tests, and the DirectX/signing subset. Exact `IPen2D` thickness, joins, and antialiasing remain a ProGPU thick-stroke shader follow-up.
- Extended the SciChart bridge with a native rect-batch path for the public Visual Xccelerator `DrawRectsBatch(XyRectVertex[], ...)` shape. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartRectVertex` mirrors the observed `float X/Y/Width/Height + uint ColorArgb` layout, `DrawRectsBatch(...)` preserves the source stream for future adapter mapping, supports top/left/center/right/bottom sprite anchors, honors axis swapping and empty clips, skips non-finite or transparent rects, and submits clipped colored triangles through the shared solid-color GPU pipeline. Focused validation covers metadata recording, invalid counts, anchor preservation, empty clips, visible-rect filtering, clipped GPU readback, SciChart-focused tests, and the DirectX/signing subset. Textured `ISprite2D` marker rendering and exact Visual Xccelerator enum/binary adapter mapping remain follow-up work.
- Extended the SciChart bridge with a native sprite-batch path for the public Visual Xccelerator `DrawSpritesBatch(XySpriteVertex[], ...)` shape. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartSpriteVertex` mirrors the observed `float X/Y + uint FillColorArgb/StrokeColorArgb` layout, `ProGpuDirectXSciChartSprite2D` wraps a Bgra8 ProGPU texture with SciChart-style pixel dimensions, and `DrawSpritesBatch(...)` preserves the source stream, honors axis swapping, `centeredAmount`, active clips, transparent/non-finite filtering, and separate fill/stroke sprite passes. Sprite draws use a blend-enabled native textured pipeline so marker alpha remains backend-owned instead of requiring WPF-managed bitmap composition. Focused validation covers metadata recording, invalid counts and centered amount, empty clips, fill/stroke draw splitting, clipped GPU readback, SciChart-focused tests, and the DirectX/signing subset. Exact `ISprite2D` binary adapter mapping and higher-volume instanced sprite submission remain follow-up work.
- Extended the SciChart bridge with native financial-series batches for the public Visual Xccelerator `DrawCandlesBatch(XohlcCandleVertex[], ...)` and `DrawOhlcBatch(XohlcCandleVertex[], ...)` shapes. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartOhlcCandleVertex` mirrors the observed `float X/O/H/L/C + uint FillColorArgb/StrokeColorArgb` layout, candle batches emit native filled bodies plus wick/body outlines, and OHLC batches emit native wick/open/close line ticks with the source stream, width, transform, `isDigital`, and `isVerticalChart` flags preserved for future adapter mapping. Focused validation covers metadata recording, invalid counts and widths, empty clips, draw splitting, clipped GPU candle fill readback, clipped GPU OHLC line readback, SciChart-focused tests, and the DirectX/signing subset. Exact pen thickness/antialiasing and deeper vertical-chart/digital financial-series semantics remain native follow-up work.
- Extended the SciChart bridge with native mountain and band batches for the public Visual Xccelerator `DrawMountainBatch(XyyBandVertex[], ...)` and `DrawBandsBatch(XyyBandVertex[], ...)` shapes. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartBandVertex` mirrors the `X/Y0/Y1` stream, `ProGpuDirectXSciChartBrush2D` and `ProGpuDirectXSciChartPalette` preserve fill/line color metadata, mountain batches fill between Y0/Y1 and draw the Y0 line, and band batches split positive/negative fill triangles at Y0/Y1 crossings before drawing both Y0 and Y1 lines. Focused validation covers metadata recording, invalid counts, empty clips, crossing-split vertex counts, GPU-backed mountain fill readback, SciChart-focused tests, and the DirectX/signing subset. Exact palette interpolation and binary Visual Xccelerator adapter mapping remain native follow-up work.
- Extended the SciChart bridge with native base `IRenderContext2D` primitives needed by axes, annotations, backgrounds, and non-batch overlay paths. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartPoint`, `ProGpuDirectXSciChartAreaSegment`, and `ProGpuDirectXSciChartPrimitiveDraw` preserve the call metadata, while `DrawLine`, `DrawLines`, `DrawEllipse`, `DrawQuad`, `FillRectangle`, `FillPolygon`, and `FillArea` submit clipped solid-color line or triangle-list work through ProGPU instead of managed WPF tessellation. Focused validation covers primitive metadata, invalid range/opacity handling, empty clips, thick-quad expansion, and GPU-backed clipped fill readback. Exact text primitives remain native follow-up work.
- Improved SciChart primitive `FillPolygon(...)` from convex-only triangle fans to simple concave polygon ear clipping inside `ProGPU.DirectX`. The path filters non-finite/duplicate points, handles clockwise and counter-clockwise winding, removes collinear vertices, and keeps hollow regions out of the submitted triangle list. Focused validation covers a GPU-backed C-shaped polygon readback where filled bars render green and the concave hollow remains clear.
- Extended SciChart primitive `DrawEllipse(...)` into native clipped solid-color ellipse fills and strokes inside `ProGPU.DirectX`. Filled ellipses emit segmented triangle fans, stroked ellipses reuse the existing one-pixel line or thick-stroke triangle expansion paths, and `ProGpuDirectXSciChartPrimitiveDraw` preserves center, pen, brush, clip, width, and height metadata for future Visual Xccelerator adapter mapping. Focused validation covers metadata, invalid center/size rejection, empty clips, fill/stroke draw splitting, and GPU-backed clipped ellipse readback.
- Extended SciChart primitive brush support from solid ARGB to native linear-gradient metadata and per-vertex GPU interpolation for filled base primitives. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartBrush2D` now preserves start/end colors plus gradient rotation, `CreateLinearGradientBrush(...)` exposes the adapter-facing factory, and rectangle, polygon, area, and ellipse fills emit gradient vertex colors through the existing native color pipeline instead of WPF-managed bitmap or tessellation workarounds. Focused validation covers gradient metadata, invalid rotation rejection, and GPU-backed red-to-green primitive fill readback.
- Extended SciChart thick-line rendering with native antialias feather geometry in `ProGPU.DirectX`. Antialiased thick pens now emit an opaque core plus transparent edge quads through the existing blend-enabled solid-color triangle pipeline, while `isAntiAliased:false` preserves the prior hard-edged quad path. The same path is reused by line batches, primitive outlines, and ellipse strokes, keeping SciChart line-series and annotation AA in ProGPU instead of WPF-managed tessellation. Focused validation covers AA versus hard-edge vertex expansion plus the DirectX/signing subset.
- Extended the SciChart bridge with native text draws in `ProGPU.DirectX`. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartFont` resolves explicit font files or cross-platform system font families through `ProGPU.Text`, `ProGpuDirectXSciChartTextDraw` preserves text, font, size, ARGB color, rotation, horizontal/vertical alignment, style flags, antialiasing intent, and active clip metadata, and GPU-backed render contexts render labels by reusing `ProGPU.Scene.Compositor`/`DrawingVisual` text paths directly into the SciChart render target with existing contents loaded. The text path flushes pending DirectX GPU commands before Scene text compositing so clears, chart primitives, labels, and later draws preserve Direct3D-style ordering. Focused validation covers metadata recording, invalid text inputs, empty clips, GPU text readback, and the SciChart-focused DirectX subset.
- Tightened DirectX HLSL conditional translation for SciChart-class shader branches. Vector-valued HLSL ternaries now lower to WGSL `select(...)` with an explicit `vecN<bool>` condition mask, avoiding invalid vector-select signatures while preserving scalar conditional lowering. A native readback test now covers vector conditional pixel output. I also re-tested `SV_IsFrontFace` as both a top-level fragment parameter and an input-struct field; the current backend still renders black for shaders declaring WGSL `front_facing`, which keeps the raw builtin capability disabled and motivated the HLSL emulation path below.
- Added ProGPU-native HLSL text `SV_IsFrontFace` emulation for DirectX triangle pipelines. Because the active backend still renders raw WGSL `front_facing` as black, `ProGPU.DirectX` now compiles front/back constant pixel shader variants and lowers one logical Direct3D draw into cull-selected WebGPU passes when the original pipeline is a solid triangle-list or triangle-strip pipeline. This keeps SciChart 3D material branches on the GPU without managed WPF workarounds. Focused readback validation covers the front-facing branch, the back-facing branch by flipping Direct3D front-face winding, and direct WGSL override variants with and without HLSL vertex-input varyings.
- Added readback validation for shader-library style pixel input structs carrying `SV_IsFrontFace`. The existing ProGPU-native emulation path now has coverage for `input.isFrontFace` branches alongside top-level fragment parameters, which better matches reusable chart material shaders.
- Tightened GPU-backed DirectX draw resource lifetimes while adding multi-pass front-facing emulation. Transient bind groups and bind-group layouts created from the active pipeline layout now stay alive until the render pass has ended and the command buffer has been submitted/released, which prevents resource-bound SciChart draw paths from hitting backend validation crashes when a helper method returns before `RenderPassEncoderEnd`.
- Fixed native buffer allocation for short GPU upload ranges and validated `UInt16` indexed DirectX front-facing draws. `GpuBuffer` now keeps its public logical size while allocating the native WebGPU buffer at the queue-write alignment, so a 6-byte DirectX index buffer can still receive the padded 8-byte upload required by the backend. A focused readback test now covers `SetIndexBuffer(... UInt16)` plus `DrawIndexed(...)` through the `SV_IsFrontFace` shader-variant emulation path used by SciChart-style 3D meshes.
- Added an explicit safety gate for order-sensitive blended `SV_IsFrontFace` emulation. `ProGPU.DirectX` now reports a front-facing emulation failure reason and fails closed for no-cull blended pipelines because the current front/back cull-pass strategy would reorder fragments. Culled blended pipelines still use the native single-sided emulation path, and focused tests cover both the fail-closed diagnostic and the supported culled-blend case.
- Applied Direct3D-style mutable draw state to the native ProGPU path. `ProGpuDirectXDeviceContext` now stores blend, depth-stencil, and rasterizer state setters, snapshots them into queued draw commands, and resolves cached WebGPU graphics-pipeline variants when the effective state or topology differs from the bound base pipeline. Draw pass setup now omits depth attachments when the effective pipeline disables depth/stencil, and WebGPU scissor is gated by the effective rasterizer state's `ScissorEnable`. The SciChart 2D and 3D bridge pipelines now explicitly opt into scissor for clipped chart draws. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 146 DirectX/SciChart tests including disabled-depth overrides, disabled-scissor stale-rect behavior, dynamic blend/write-mask state, dynamic primitive topology, and existing clipped SciChart 2D/3D readbacks.
- Added native DirectX render-target/depth-stencil binding validation and depth-only draw-pass execution in `ProGPU.DirectX`. `SetRenderTargets(...)`, RTV/DSV overloads, clears, and queued draws now validate render-target/depth-stencil usage before recording incompatible commands, GPU-backed pixel draws fail before queueing when no color target is bound, and no-pixel-shader depth-only pipelines can submit WebGPU render passes with zero color attachments. D32 depth-only passes now omit stencil load/store state by using undefined stencil attachment ops unless a D24S8 stencil-enabled pipeline is active. This supports SciChart-style depth prepasses and 3D chart setup without forcing WPF-managed dummy color targets or bridge-side validation. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 148 DirectX/SciChart tests including a depth-only prepass that rejects a later color draw through native depth testing.
- Tightened DirectX HLSL register assignment for SciChart/SharpDX-style shader source that omits explicit `register(...)` annotations. `ProGpuDirectXHlslTranslator` now assigns unannotated cbuffers and t/s/u resources to first-unused Direct3D registers in source order while preserving explicit bindings and separate SRV, sampler, and UAV register spaces. This prevents multiple unannotated cbuffers or shader resources from collapsing to slot 0 and keeps generated WGSL binding maps aligned with DirectX context snapshots. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 151 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Tightened DirectX HLSL expression and semantic lowering for shader-library style chart code. The translator now tracks parameter/local identifier scope so locals that shadow cbuffer fields are not rewritten to uniform members, emits vector-shaped WGSL bounds for vector `saturate(...)`, emits `clip(...)` discard predicates for vector parameters and locals, and assigns struct user-semantic locations per struct with Direct3D semantic indices preserved inside each semantic base. This keeps vertex-input, vertex-output, and pixel-input location namespaces separate while allowing `TEXCOORD1`/`TEXCOORD0` fields to link by semantic index instead of declaration order. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 155 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Aligned DirectX graphics-pipeline default state with Direct3D. `DxBlendStateDescriptor` now disables blending by default and `DxRasterizerStateDescriptor` now treats clockwise triangles as front-facing while keeping back-face culling as the default, so SciChart/SharpDX-style callers that omit blend/rasterizer descriptors get Direct3D-compatible behavior instead of ProGPU-specific alpha blending or counter-clockwise orientation. Front-facing emulation tests now state their non-default counter-clockwise expectation explicitly. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 156 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Tightened DirectX input-layout handling for SciChart/SharpDX-style vertex streams. Explicit input layouts now fail closed unless each element carries a shader location derived from shader-signature reflection or an explicit adapter mapping, avoiding descriptor-order fallback that can swap Direct3D semantics. GPU-backed pipelines remap non-contiguous Direct3D input-slot numbers to compact backend vertex-buffer slots at draw time, so callers can bind original slots like slot 1 without repacking vertex streams or losing vertex data. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 158 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Aligned more DirectX pipeline and shader defaults for SciChart/SharpDX-style callers. `DxDepthStencilStateDescriptor` now defaults to Direct3D-compatible depth enabled, depth writes on, and `Less` comparison, while color-only pipelines with no depth format still omit backend depth state. HLSL top-level entry-point parameters now assign user-semantic locations from the full semantic base/index map, so valid signatures such as `POSITION0` plus `TEXCOORD0` no longer emit duplicate WGSL locations. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 159 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Added HLSL constant-buffer packing preservation in `ProGPU.DirectX` for SciChart/SharpDX shader-library code. Constant buffers whose HLSL register/component offsets cannot be represented by WGSL's natural uniform member alignment now lower to packed `vec4<u32>` registers, and field reads reconstruct scalar, vector, and matrix values from the original Direct3D register components. Natural-layout buffers still use normal WGSL structs. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 161 DirectX/SciChart tests including GPU readback from a `float`, `float2`, `float` packed register.
- Extended the SciChart line-series bridge to honor `XyColorVertex.Offset` natively inside `ProGPU.DirectX`. Thin, thick, antialiased, strip, pair, and digital line expansion now applies each vertex offset along the segment normal before submitting WebGPU line or triangle geometry, preserving Visual Xccelerator line streams without managed WPF/SciChart adapter rewrites. Focused validation includes `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SciChart" --no-restore`, covering 44 SciChart tests with GPU readback from an offset thick line, and `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 162 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Extended DirectX `Texture2D.Map(...)` for SciChart/SharpDX-style array texture staging. Single-mip array textures now map individual array-slice subresources with Direct3D-style subresource offsets, preserve row/depth pitch metadata, update CPU shadow storage at the mapped slice, and upload only the mapped native array layer after mapped-slice writes. Mipmapped and multisampled mappings still fail closed. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 164 DirectX/SciChart tests, plus a targeted `GpuTexture.WritePixelsSubRect(...)` array-layer upload regression.
- Extended DirectX and backend texture staging to wider native WebGPU formats used by SciChart/SharpDX-style resources. `GpuTexture` now computes compact pixel strides from the actual WebGPU texture format for uploads, sub-rect writes, array-layer writes, and readback instead of assuming unknown formats are 4 bytes per pixel. `ProGPU.DirectX` maps RG32 and RGBA32 float/uint/sint texture formats to native WebGPU formats, preserves R16/RG32/RGBA32 row/depth pitches during `Texture2D.Map(...)`, and keeps unsupported three-component texture formats fail-closed rather than silently mapping them to BGRA8. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 172 DirectX/SciChart tests, plus `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~GpuTextureWritePixelsAndReadPixelsUseNativeFormatStride" --no-restore`.
- Extended DirectX `Texture2D.Map(...)` for SciChart/SharpDX-style mipmapped staging resources. CPU-shadow and metadata textures now allocate compact storage for every mip level in every array slice, use Direct3D subresource indexing (`mip + arraySlice * mipLevels`), preserve per-mip row/depth pitches for power-of-two and non-power-of-two textures, expose the mapped subresource index, and reject out-of-range subresources deterministically. Follow-up native texture work added ProGPU backend mip-chain allocation, explicit mip-level sub-rect uploads, all-mip texture copies, and per-mip readback for GPU-backed color textures, so mapped DirectX writes now upload the selected array/mip subresource through WebGPU instead of forcing a single native mip. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TextureMap" --no-restore`, covering 20 texture-map tests, and `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 179 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Added CPU-shadow depth texture mapping for SciChart/SharpDX-style 3D resources. `Texture2D.Map(...)` now supports `D32Float` and `D24UnormS8UInt` staging/readback with 4-byte compact pitch metadata, including mapped mip subresources, while GPU-backed depth mapping fails closed until native backend depth staging is implemented. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TextureMap" --no-restore`, covering 19 texture-map tests, and `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 179 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Added DirectX HLSL comparison-sampler translation for SciChart/SharpDX-style 3D shader libraries. `SamplerComparisonState`, `Texture2D.SampleCmp(...)`, and `Texture2D.SampleCmpLevelZero(...)` now stay inside `ProGPU.DirectX`: comparison-sampled textures emit WGSL `texture_depth_2d`/`texture_depth_2d_array`, comparison samplers emit `sampler_comparison`, and calls lower to `textureSampleCompare(...)`. Follow-up GPU-backed validation now clears a native `D32Float` depth texture, binds it as an SRV with a comparison sampler, executes an HLSL `SampleCmp`/`SampleCmpLevelZero` pixel draw through WebGPU, and verifies the expected pass/fail compare channels from texture readback. A GPU-backed depth map/write/readback experiment was attempted for `D32Float`, but both queue-write and padded buffer-copy staging read back zero through the backend; later work verified read-only `D32Float` depth mapping while keeping CPU depth write/upload fail-closed. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 181 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Added native DirectX `Texture3D` support for SciChart/SharpDX-style volume, surface, and heatmap resource paths. `GpuTexture` now supports WebGPU `Dimension3D` allocation, views, volume uploads, per-mip readback, and depth-aware copies; `ProGPU.DirectX` exposes `DxTexture3DDescriptor`, `CreateTexture3D(...)`, `Texture3D` SRVs, 3D mapped subresources with Direct3D row/depth pitch, GPU-backed map/unmap uploads, and HLSL `Texture3D.Sample(...)`/`Load(...)` lowering to WGSL `texture_3d` resource calls. Focused validation is `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Texture3D" --no-restore`, covering 3 Texture3D tests, and `dotnet test src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --filter DirectXShimTests --no-restore`, covering 184 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Added the first WPF SDK SciChart MVP sample at `samples/ProGPU.Wpf.SciChartMvpApp`. The app keeps the no-source-change SDK shape (`<Project Sdk="ProGPU.Wpf.Sdk/11.0.0-dev">`) and renders 2D line/mountain/column/candle/heatmap primitives plus a 3D surface/point-cloud through the reusable `ProGPU.DirectX` SciChart bridge into a WPF `WriteableBitmap`. `eng/run-progpu-wpf-scichart.sh`, `PROGPU_WPF_SCICHART_VALIDATE=1`, `PROGPU_WPF_SCICHART_RUN_VALIDATE=1`, package-mode SDK CI, and the managed project graph guard now cover the sample. The commercial `SciChart`/`SciChart3D` package adapter remains open because licensed assemblies are not present in this workspace; the MVP proves the ProGPU DirectX render context path that the future adapter should call.
- Fixed the SciChart MVP heatmap resource lifetime so Float32 height and gradient textures survive until the recorded DirectX draw commands are flushed. The failure was diagnosed through new ProGPU.DirectX bind-group diagnostics that report the exact cbuffer/SRV/sampler snapshot when native bind-group creation fails. Focused validation now passes for `PROGPU_WPF_SCICHART_VALIDATE=1 ./eng/run-progpu-wpf-scichart.sh`, `PROGPU_WPF_SCICHART_RUN_VALIDATE=1 ./eng/run-progpu-wpf-scichart.sh`, and the SDK switch runtime smoke after refreshing the local `ProGPU.DirectX` package cache. The managed graph test builds, but VSTest execution is currently blocked in this environment because the generated `net10.0` testhost is forced to the repo-local `.dotnet` runtime that contains only .NET 11 preview.
- Added native SciChart 3D line-list/line-strip execution to `ProGPU.DirectX` for axes, grids, and line-series style workloads. The render context now records `ProGpuDirectXSciChartLine3DDraw`, validates strip/list vertex rules, submits WebGPU line-list or line-strip draws through the same 3D camera/depth/scissor path as surface meshes and point clouds, and the WPF SciChart MVP sample now exercises and counts a 3D line strip alongside surface and point draws. Focused validation includes direct VSTest execution of `FlushSubmitsGpuBackedSciChart3DLineCommandsWithClip` plus `SciChartRenderContext3DRecordsPointCloudAndTriangleMesh`, direct VSTest execution of `ProGpuWpfSdkProvidesSwitchOnlyPackagingSurface`, `PROGPU_WPF_SCICHART_VALIDATE=1 ./eng/run-progpu-wpf-scichart.sh`, and `PROGPU_WPF_SCICHART_RUN_VALIDATE=1 ./eng/run-progpu-wpf-scichart.sh`; `dotnet test` remains blocked by the repo `global.json` MTP/VSTest mismatch for these projects, so direct VSTest with runtime roll-forward is the current local test path.
- Added Direct3D-style `GenerateMips(...)` support to `ProGPU.DirectX` for SciChart/SharpDX-style color texture chains. Default texture SRVs now span the full mip/array range, immediate contexts record `GenerateMips` commands, `Texture2D` resources keep per-subresource shadow-current metadata, supported RGBA/BGRA SRV ranges generate lower mips inside the DirectX shim, generated levels upload back to native ProGPU textures, and GPU-rendered source mips synchronize from backend memory when the texture has copy-source usage. Native clear/draw execution now marks render targets dirty and honors RTV/DSV texture views for clear/draw attachments, which prevents mip generation and readback from using stale upload shadows. Focused validation is direct VSTest execution of `FullyQualifiedName~GenerateMips`, covering 3 metadata/GPU-backed mip tests, and direct VSTest execution of `FullyQualifiedName~DirectXShimTests`, covering 188 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Moved GPU-backed DirectX `GenerateMips(...)` onto a native ProGPU render-pass shader path. `GpuTexture.GenerateMipmaps2DLinear(...)` creates single-mip texture views, samples each previous 2D mip into the next mip with a fullscreen WebGPU pass, supports requested SRV mip/array ranges, and releases temporary shader, sampler, bind-group layout, pipeline layout, pipeline, encoder, command buffer, bind groups, and texture views through failure-safe cleanup. `ProGpuDirectXTexture2D.GenerateMips(...)` now prefers that backend path for GPU-backed RGBA/BGRA textures, so SciChart/SharpDX render-target SRVs can generate mips without `CopyDestination` usage or CPU shadow upload workarounds; the compact CPU/metadata downsampler remains only for non-backend resources. Focused validation is direct VSTest execution of `FullyQualifiedName~GenerateMips`, covering 3 metadata/GPU-backed mip tests including a rendered source without copy-destination usage, and direct VSTest execution of `FullyQualifiedName~DirectXShimTests`, covering 188 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Cached the native mip-generation shader resources in ProGPU for SciChart-style repeated texture work. `GpuTexture` now keeps one `WgpuContext`-scoped mip-generator cache with shared shader, sampler, bind-group layout, pipeline layout, and per-`TextureFormat` render pipelines, releasing the cached native objects through `WgpuContext.Disposing` and the existing deferred disposal queues. Repeated `GenerateMips(...)` calls across multiple render-target textures now avoid recreating the render pipeline while still creating per-mip views and bind groups for the active source/destination slices. Focused validation is direct VSTest execution of `FullyQualifiedName~GenerateMips`, covering 4 metadata/GPU-backed/cache-reuse mip tests, and direct VSTest execution of `FullyQualifiedName~DirectXShimTests`, covering 189 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Added Direct3D-style color MSAA array-subresource resolve support in `ProGPU.DirectX`. Multisampled `Texture2D` arrays are now backed by one native multisampled 2D texture per DirectX array slice, because WebGPU does not expose the same MSAA texture-array render-target shape directly. RTV/DSV construction and clear/draw/resolve execution select the correct native slice texture, resolve views target one mip/slice, broad multi-slice MSAA views fail closed before native view creation, and focused coverage validates layer 0/layer 1 clear, draw, and resolve readback. Focused validation is direct VSTest execution of `FullyQualifiedName~Resolve`, covering 19 resolve tests, and direct VSTest execution of `FullyQualifiedName~DirectXShimTests`, covering 192 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Added verified GPU-backed `D32Float` depth read staging for SciChart/SharpDX-style 3D inspection paths. `GpuTexture` now uses `DepthOnly` texture-copy aspects for depth uploads/readbacks/copies, and `Texture2D.Map(Read)` allows native `D32Float` depth textures after GPU clear/draw work while write maps and packed `D24UnormS8UInt` maps fail closed. A fresh CPU depth-upload attempt using queue writes and padded buffer-to-depth copies still read back zero on this backend, so CPU depth write/upload remains an explicit native backend gap rather than a managed WPF workaround. Focused validation is direct VSTest execution of `FullyQualifiedName~GpuBackedD32FloatTextureReadMapUsesBackendDepthStaging|FullyQualifiedName~GpuBackedDepthTextureWriteMapFailsClosedUntilDepthUploadIsValidated`, covering 3 depth-map tests, and direct VSTest execution of `FullyQualifiedName~DirectXShimTests`, covering 194 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Added native SciChart 3D triangle-strip execution to `ProGPU.DirectX`. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartRenderContext3D.DrawTriangleStrip(...)` records SciChart-facing strip metadata, shares the 3D camera/depth/scissor path with surface meshes, point clouds, and line strips, and submits native WebGPU `TriangleStrip` draws without managed WPF tessellation. The WPF SciChart MVP sample now exercises and counts a translucent 3D strip in addition to the existing surface, point-cloud, and line-strip paths. Focused validation is direct VSTest execution of the SciChart 3D strip/line/surface tests plus `FullyQualifiedName~DirectXShimTests`, covering 195 DirectX/SciChart tests.
- Added an opt-in real SciChart package lane to `samples/ProGPU.Wpf.SciChartMvpApp`. Setting `PROGPU_WPF_SCICHART_REAL_PACKAGES=1` or `-p:ProGpuWpfUseRealSciChartPackages=true` restores `SciChart` and `SciChart3D` package version `9.0.0.29196`, reads `SCICHART_RUNTIME_LICENSE_KEY` at startup, calls `SciChartSurface.SetRuntimeLicenseKey(...)` without embedding the license in source, validates real `XyDataSeries`/`XyzDataSeries3D` usage, and attempts to construct real 2D/3D SciChart controls beside the ProGPU DirectX-rendered MVP surface. On macOS the NuGet payload has no `runtimes/osx-*` native assets and the assemblies reference Windows DLL/Direct3D payload names instead, so the sample reports that native runtime gap while still validating package restore, compile, license setup, and data API compatibility. This proves the SDK can consume the real packages now, while the remaining adapter work is the native SciChart runtime/binary entry-point bridge into `ProGPU.DirectX`. The local development machine stores the runtime license in Keychain and exports it through `SCICHART_RUNTIME_LICENSE_KEY` for new shells.
- Added native SciChart colored-sprite marker execution to `ProGPU.DirectX`. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartRenderContext2D.DrawColoredSprites(...)` mirrors the public Visual Xccelerator `DrawColoredSprites(ISprite2D, ColoredVertex[], startIndex, count)` shape with neutral `X/Y/ColorArgb` vertices, preserves SciChart start/count range semantics, validates Bgra8 sprite resources, honors axis swapping, `centeredAmount`, sampler choice, active clipping, transparent/non-finite filtering, and submits blend-enabled textured marker quads through the GPU path. Follow-up work moved those colored markers from CPU-expanded six-vertex quads to a native instanced marker pipeline: slot 0 carries a cached six-corner quad, slot 1 carries one NDC rectangle plus ARGB tint per marker, and the DirectX shim submits `DrawInstanced(6, markerCount)` so high-volume point markers avoid managed-side quad expansion. The SciChart MVP sample now draws colored 2D markers through this API, and focused metadata plus GPU-backed readback coverage proves clipped native tinting without a managed WPF bitmap workaround.
- Fixed a Silk.NET input-context ownership issue hit by the package-mode SDK smoke after cursor updates. `SilkNetWpfInputService` now tracks the `IInputContext` it creates for each Silk view, and `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` reuses that attached context when setting cursors instead of asking the cursor service to create a second context for the same window. This keeps mouse/keyboard input and cursor updates on one Silk.NET input owner and avoids the `More than one input context for window` failure in external SDK samples. The generated external no-source-change SDK apphost live-input validation budget was also raised for cold package-mode startup; the focused external SDK smoke now passes after rebuilding the generated app.
- Hardened package-mode SDK CI cleanup for mutable `11.0.0-dev` packages. The rebuilt package validation exposed an old `ProGPU.Wpf.HelloApp` per-app NuGet cache that did not restore the newly required `ProGPU.DirectX` package, causing a shutdown-time `FileNotFoundException` after `Application.Run` validation had already passed. `eng/progpu-wpf-sdk-ci.sh` now clears the Hello app package cache alongside its bin/obj output so SDK-switched apps regenerate restore graphs when the ProGPU package surface changes.
- Revalidated the current minimal DirectX/SciChart handoff before returning to WPF-port work. The ProGPU branch already contains the NativeAOT facade project emitter plus reflected ABI/source scaffold, and the DirectX shim subset passes through VSTest with 216 tests under the workspace .NET runtime roll-forward. Full real SciChart control execution remains blocked on proprietary licensing/native-engine exports and stays out of the next WPF compatibility slice.
- Returned from the minimal DirectX/SciChart scaffold lane to the SDK/Xceed compatibility lane. The generated external no-source-change SDK app now compiles and validates additional managed Xceed Toolkit surfaces from a normal `Extended.Wpf.Toolkit` package reference: `RichTextBox` with `PlainTextFormatter`, `MultiLineTextEditor`, `ButtonSpinner`, and a two-page `Wizard`/`WizardPage` flow with page-change, finish, and cancel routed events. This extends the SDK-only migration gate without adding app-side ProGPU APIs or WPF-managed workarounds.
- Extended the same external SDK/Xceed gate through a non-modal Toolkit windowing primitive. The generated no-source-change app now declares `WindowContainer` plus `WindowControl`, validates caption/style/border/thickness/visibility/text bindings, applies the Toolkit template, exercises activation, header click/drag routed events, close-button handling, and restores visibility during `Application.Run()`. This moves another managed Xceed windowing surface onto the SDK-only migration path while leaving full `ChildWindow` modal timing as a separate follow-up.
- Strengthened the SDK-switch custom SDK deliverable through a referenced WPF control-library resource/theme lane. `ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchLibrary` now contributes a normal component `ResourceDictionary`, `ThemeInfo`, and `Themes/Generic.xaml` default style for a library-owned custom control. The SDK-switched app merges `/ProGPU.Wpf.SdkSwitchLibrary;component/Resources/LibraryResources.xaml`, consumes the library brush/string/thickness resources, instantiates the library themed control with no ProGPU-specific project items, and the runtime harness validates cross-assembly BAML resource lookup plus the library `Generic.xaml` template and `ComponentResourceKey` brush.

- Removed runtime type-name diagnostics from the Hello and MVP SDK sample validations. `DescribeInputElement(...)` now reports stable element names or neutral input labels, MVP navigation/drag/resize diagnostics no longer use `GetType().Name`, selected-date validation fails with a semantic message, and dispatcher synchronization-context checks use typed pattern matching instead of runtime type inspection. The SDK graph guard now rejects `GetType()` in both sample code-behind files so no-source-change SDK validation does not normalize reflection-style diagnostics. - Moved exact local rectangle `PathGeometry` draw replay onto primitive rectangle commands. Generated drawing contexts, object render-data replay, and `GeometryDrawing` replay now reuse the existing exact rectangle path reader to lower identity-transformed closed/fill axis-aligned rectangle paths to `DrawNativeRectangle(...)` or compatibility `DrawRectangle(...)` before generic geometry adaptation, while transformed/non-rectangle/incomplete paths still route through the generic geometry path. Current de-reflection status: `src/ProGPU.Wpf` remains reflection-marker and type-name-diagnostic clean; remaining cleanup is still fallback reduction for arbitrary path/tile/effect/bitmap replay plus broader reused WPF/XAML framework reflection outside the ProGPU bridge hot path. Validation passed `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD_TO_PRERELEASE=1 dotnet build src/ProGPU.Wpf.Tests/ProGPU.Wpf.Tests.csproj --no-restore -v:minimal /p:UseSharedCompilation=false`, focused rectangle-path/graph VSTest with 4 tests, full `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` with 876 tests, product reflection-marker audit, and Toolkit plus paid Xceed sample builds.
- Moved exact local line `PathGeometry` draw replay onto primitive line commands. The new `WpfMediaLineGeometryReader` shares finite identity `LineGeometry` detection and conservatively recognizes one-figure, non-closed, single stroked `LineSegment` path geometry; generated drawing contexts, object render-data replay, and `GeometryDrawing` replay now lower those path strokes to `DrawNativeLine(...)` or compatibility `DrawLine(...)` before generic geometry adaptation. - Added a real-package-facing SciChart `ColoredVertex` bridge to `ProGPU.DirectX`. Metadata inspection of `SciChart.Drawing.dll`/`SciChart.Data.dll` confirmed the public `IExtremeRenderContext2D.DrawLineStrip(IPen2D, ColoredVertex[], startIndex, count)` and `DrawColoredSprites(ISprite2D, ColoredVertex[], startIndex, count)` contracts, with `ColoredVertex` exposing `X`, `Y`, `U`, and `ColorArgb`. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartColoredVertex` now mirrors that shape, `DrawLineStrip(...)` maps it into the native line-strip path using `U` as the per-vertex offset, `DrawColoredSprites(...)` maps it into the existing instanced sprite-marker path, and the SciChart MVP sample now exercises those adapter-facing overloads instead of only the ProGPU-internal batch structs. This keeps the real SciChart WPF adapter path in reusable ProGPU code while the proprietary native runtime/binary entry-point bridge remains open.
- Added native SciChart vertical pixel strip execution to `ProGPU.DirectX`. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartRenderContext2D.DrawPixelsVertically(...)` now covers uniform `x/y/color-run` strips by uploading a transient 1-pixel-wide Bgra8 texture and drawing one clipped native textured quad, and covers coordinate-driven y runs by submitting clipped solid-color quads through the existing fill pipeline. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartVerticalPixelsDraw` preserves source colors, y coordinates, opacity, uniform mode, y-axis flip, and active clip metadata for future real Visual Xccelerator adapter mapping. The SciChart MVP sample now draws vertical palette/run strips through both overloads, and focused metadata plus GPU-backed readback tests prove the path renders inside the active clip without a WPF-managed bitmap workaround.
- Addressed another active ProGPU PR #17 DirectX review batch in the native shim. `ProGPU.DirectX` now treats DirectX RGBA/BGRA texture resources as straight-alpha uploads by default, matching Direct3D clear/upload semantics for SciChart and SharpDX surfaces, and rejects scalar input-layout formats such as `R8Unorm` and `R16Float` as vertex attributes because WebGPU has no one-component equivalent with matching stride. Focused validation covers scalar layout rejection and GPU-backed straight-alpha texture allocation, and the full `DirectXShimTests` suite now passes with 203 tests.
- Addressed the ProGPU PR #17 texture CPU-access review batch. `ProGPU.DirectX` now folds `DxCpuAccessFlags.Read` into backend `CopySrc` texture usage and `DxCpuAccessFlags.Write` into backend `CopyDst` usage, including array-slice and 3D texture allocation paths, and shadow synchronization treats CPU-readable textures as effective copy-source resources. Focused validation covers GPU-backed CPU-readable render-target readback without explicit `CopySource` and CPU-writable shader-texture uploads without explicit `CopyDestination`; the full `DirectXShimTests` suite now passes with 205 tests.
- Added native SciChart 3D XYZ data-series bridge paths to `ProGPU.DirectX`. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartXyzPoint3D`, `ProGpuDirectXSciChartXyzSeries3DOptions`, `DrawXyzDataSeriesLineStrip(...)`, `DrawXyzDataSeriesPointCloud(...)`, and `DrawXyzDataSeriesRibbon(...)` map real `XyzDataSeries3D<double>`-shaped data into normalized native 3D vertices and a triangle-strip ribbon path for reliable WebGPU rasterization. The WPF SciChart MVP now reuses the same sample XYZ data in both the default bridge renderer and the real-package lane, validates visible 3D bridge pixels, and keeps this work in ProGPU instead of managed WPF bitmap fallbacks. Focused validation covers the XYZ line/point/ribbon metadata path, GPU-backed SciChart 3D draws, and the full `DirectXShimTests` suite now passes with 207 tests.

The current `SciChart`/`SciChart3D` `9.0.0.29196` packages restore and compile in the SDK sample, but package inspection shows only `lib/net462` and `lib/net6.0-windows7.0` assets and no `runtimes/osx-*` native payload. The restored assemblies reference Windows payloads such as `AbtLicensingNative.dll`, `VXccelEngine3D.dll`, `d3d9.dll`, `d3d11.dll`, `dxgi.dll`, and `D3DCOMPILER_47.dll`, matching SciChart's WPF install docs that describe the 3D assembly as a mixed .NET/C++ component requiring the VC++ runtime. `PROGPU_WPF_SCICHART_REAL_PACKAGES=1 PROGPU_WPF_SCICHART_VALIDATE=1 ./eng/run-progpu-wpf-scichart.sh` now passes by validating package restore, license setup through `SCICHART_RUNTIME_LICENSE_KEY`, real 2D/3D data-series APIs, and the ProGPU-native 3D bridge snapshot, then reporting the real control construction as a Windows native runtime gap. The remaining durable task is not adding a macOS NuGet package; it is implementing a ProGPU-hosted ABI/native-engine facade for SciChart licensing, Visual Xccelerator/`VXccelEngine3D`, and Direct3D entry points on top of `ProGPU.DirectX`.
- Added a native SciChart 3D waterfall/slice bridge path to `ProGPU.DirectX`. `ProGpuDirectXSciChartWaterfall3DOptions`, `ProGpuDirectXSciChartWaterfall3DDraw`, and `DrawWaterfallDataSeries(...)` now accept row/column height fields, normalize chart coordinates, generate palette-colored vertical slice vertices and index buffers, and submit depth-tested clipped triangle-list work through the DirectX/WebGPU path. The WPF SciChart MVP renderer and real-package fallback snapshot now exercise that path alongside surface mesh, XYZ line/ribbon/point, and triangle-strip draws, keeping surface/waterfall 3D chart bring-up in ProGPU rather than managed WPF mesh or bitmap workarounds.
- Added a reusable native dependency inventory to `ProGPU.DirectX` for the SciChart real-package lane. `ProGpuDirectXNativeDependencyInspector` reflects managed assemblies for `[DllImport]` declarations and also scans assembly string metadata for dynamic native module names such as `VXccelEngine3D.dll`, without loading or invoking those native libraries. The real SciChart MVP sample now reports the detected native dependencies in validation output and fallback UI text, so the current macOS failure is recorded as an ABI/native-engine compatibility list for the future ProGPU DirectX facade instead of a vague missing-runtime error.
- Added native compatibility classification on top of that inventory. `ProGpuDirectXNativeCompatibilityPlanner` maps detected modules into ProGPU native facade work (`AbtLicensingNative`, Visual Xccelerator/`VXccelEngine3D`, Direct3D, DXGI, D3DCompiler), host OS Win32 abstraction work (`USER32`, `KERNEL32`, `GDI32`, `ADVAPI32`, `OLE32`, `mscoree`), managed SciChart assembly hints, and unknown modules that need inspection. The real SciChart MVP validation now prints this classified plan so the next work can implement the missing native ABI surfaces in ProGPU rather than treating every `.dll` string as an equally actionable runtime dependency.
- Added a reusable native resolver/facade hook for the real SciChart package lane. `ProGpuDirectXNativeResolver` can register a `NativeLibrary.SetDllImportResolver` for SciChart assemblies, classify requested modules through the compatibility plan, load a configured future facade from `PROGPU_DIRECTX_NATIVE_FACADE_PATH` or per-module `PROGPU_DIRECTX_NATIVE_FACADE_MODULES`, and otherwise return zero while recording `facade not configured` or load-failure diagnostics. The WPF SciChart MVP installs this resolver before `SciChartSurface.SetRuntimeLicenseKey(...)`, so license/native-engine/Direct3D load attempts are observable from the first P/Invoke without pretending unsupported proprietary exports are implemented. This confirms the current macOS failure is not a missing SciChart NuGet runtime package; the missing deliverable is the ProGPU-native ABI facade itself.

The real SciChart MVP now reports exact known exports in validation output, so the native facade work can start from concrete symbols such as the SciChart licensing and Win32 imports observed from `SciChart.Core` while still tracking Visual Xccelerator engine modules whose export surface requires runtime probing or binary analysis.

This gives the future ProGPU native facade generator enough managed evidence to implement or stub exports deliberately instead of relying on symbol names alone.
