Full real SciChart control execution remains blocked by proprietary Windows native ABI exports, so the next implementation slices should stay on WPF SDK, managed-framework reuse, windowing/input/rendering, Toolkit/AvalonDock, XAML, themes, and custom-SDK delivery rather than adding managed SciChart workarounds.
- Returned to the no-source-change WPF SDK lane by extending the generated default-item external app through common file/folder dialogs. The switch-only app now imports normal `Microsoft.Win32` dialog APIs, registers the existing portable file-dialog service, and validates `OpenFileDialog`, owner `SaveFileDialog`, and owner `OpenFolderDialog` results during `Application.Run()` without explicit project items or ProGPU app code. `dotnet build src/ProGPU.Wpf.SdkExternalSmokeHarness/ProGPU.Wpf.SdkExternalSmokeHarness.csproj --no-restore --verbosity minimal` and `dotnet run --project src/ProGPU.Wpf.SdkExternalSmokeHarness/ProGPU.Wpf.SdkExternalSmokeHarness.csproj --no-build -v:minimal` both pass.
- Extended the same default-item SDK platform-service lane through `MessageBox` and `PrintDialog`. The generated switch-only app now registers the deterministic portable message-box service, validates no-owner and owner `MessageBox.Show(...)` overloads, and validates non-Windows `PrintDialog` page-range metadata, null portable queue, fallback ticket, printable area defaults, and fail-closed `ShowDialog()` result during `Application.Run()`. The focused harness build and external no-source-change SDK smoke both pass again.
- Extended the generated default-item SDK app through direct public `Clipboard` and `DataObject` APIs in addition to the existing rich-text command coverage. The switch-only app now validates text clipboard state, `GetDataObject`, `IsCurrent`, `Flush`, custom `DataObject` formats, typed `TryGetData(...)`, file-drop-list round trips, and clear semantics during `Application.Run()`, keeping clipboard ownership in managed WPF while ProGPU/Silk.NET supplies the portable platform service.
- Added the commercial Xceed Toolkit Plus/DataGrid MVP sample at `samples/ProGPU.Wpf.XceedPaidApp`. The app uses the normal `ProGPU.Wpf.Sdk/11.0.0-dev` project shape, direct paid Toolkit/AvalonDock package references, and the separate `Xceed.Products.Wpf.DataGrid.Full` product package. The direct package split is intentional because the Toolkit metapackage also brings the Toolkit-era DataGrid assembly, which collides with the commercial `Xceed.Wpf.DataGrid.DataGridControl` type. Runtime licensing is env-only through `XCEED_TOOLKIT_LICENSE_KEY` and `XCEED_DATAGRID_LICENSE_KEY`; the repository stores only variable names and licenser API calls. The sample hosts Toolkit Plus Material controls, AvalonDock Windows10 theme, and a paid Xceed `DataGridControl` document backed by 100,000 rows with `DataGridCollectionViewSource`, explicit columns, `TableView`, fixed headers, row selection, and `BringItemIntoView(...)` navigation. `PROGPU_WPF_XCEED_PAID_VALIDATE=1 ./eng/run-progpu-wpf-xceed-paid.sh` validates package restore and paid assembly surface without constructing licensed controls when local env vars are absent. Restore currently reports advisory warnings from Xceed transitive `System.Data.SqlClient` 4.7.0 and `System.Drawing.Common` 5.0.1 packages.
- Moved another clipping/performance piece into ProGPU instead of WPF managed sample code. `ProGPU.Scene` now clips non-rotated texture quads against active rectangular clips before upload while preserving the original source-rectangle UV range by bilinear interpolation, so image/layer/source-rect draws trim geometry in the compositor without rewriting WPF or third-party control visuals. Focused ProGPU validation covers a clipped source-rect texture draw and proves the uploaded quad, UVs, and rendered pixels remain correct.
- Expanded the paid Xceed DataGrid MVP beyond basic table construction. The sample now configures `DataGridCollectionViewSource` with explicit item properties, active-row filtering, category grouping, updated-date sorting, auto-filter/filter-row mode, count/average stat functions, `StatRow`/`StatCell` fixed footers, a group footer, ThemePack 1 `Office2007BlueTheme`, auto-created detail descriptions, an explicit `DetailConfiguration`, and lazy per-row details so the 100k-row workload keeps detail data cheap until expanded. Package-surface validation now also loads paid DataGrid stats/detail/theme, Views3D `CardflowView3D`/`ElementalBlackTheme`, and Workbooks exporter types without embedding or printing license values.
- Expanded the paid Xceed DataGrid MVP through another commercial-manager slice. The sample now exercises merged headers, `MergedColumnManagerRow`, `SearchControl`/`SearchText`, built-in CSV and Excel export commands, in-memory `SaveUserSettings(...)`/`LoadUserSettings(...)`, `TableflowView`, and user-triggered `CardflowView3D` activation through normal Xceed APIs. Package-surface validation now checks DataGrid export, settings, column chooser/search, merged-header, Tableflow/TreeGridflow, Views3D, and Workbooks types plus the public `DataGridControl` export/settings methods. Export paths remain env/config driven through `PROGPU_WPF_XCEED_PAID_EXPORT_DIR`; no license values are stored in source.
- Added a paid Xceed DataGrid virtualization document to the MVP sample. `DataGridVirtualizingQueryableCollectionViewSource` now binds to the same 100k-row model as an `IQueryable`, with bounded `PageSize`, `MaxRealizedItemCount`, deferred item scrolling, and explicit columns in a second AvalonDock document. Validation checks the virtualizing collection view/source/panel types and runtime source/grid metadata when license variables are present, keeping data virtualization in managed Xceed/WPF while renderer performance work remains in ProGPU.
- Added paid Xceed DataGrid column-chooser and visible-column coverage. The commercial sample now hosts the real `ColumnChooserControl`, binds it to the paid grid's `Columns`, enables `AllowColumnChooser` with `ColumnChooserSortOrder`, marks the fixed Id column out of the chooser with `ShowInColumnChooser`, and exposes a command that toggles the Status column through `ColumnBase.Visible` while reporting `VisibleColumns.Count`. Validation checks the chooser/context-menu package surface and runtime visible-column mutation, keeping column manager behavior in reused Xceed/WPF code instead of ProGPU-side DataGrid policy.
- Added paid Xceed DataGrid unbound/computed-column coverage. The commercial sample now declares a `DataGridUnboundItemProperty` named `PriorityBand`, computes values in the package `QueryValue` event, exposes the result through an `UnboundColumn`, includes that field in the merged execution header, and validates `DataGridItemPropertyBase.GetValue(...)` dispatch plus query-event execution. This keeps computed item-property behavior in managed Xceed/WPF while ProGPU remains responsible for rendering, invalidation, clipping, and shader performance.
- Added paid Xceed DataGrid editing and validation coverage. The commercial sample now includes a separate editable `DataGridControl` document with `ReadOnly=False`, `EditTriggers=CellIsCurrent`, `CellEditorDisplayConditions`, mutable `INotifyPropertyChanged`/`IDataErrorInfo` rows, and runtime self-test checks for score validation without using Xceed's obsolete `ValidationMode` property. Package-surface validation also checks Xceed cell editor, validation-context, validation-error, row-validation, and validation-rule types, keeping edit/validation policy in managed Xceed/WPF instead of adding ProGPU-side grid state.
- Moved the real WPF non-Windows `PathGeometry.GetPathBoundsAsRB(...)` fallback onto ProGPU-owned vector helpers. `PresentationCore` now source-includes the small `ProGPU.Vector` bounds set as internal implementation code, converts parsed WPF figures/segments into `ProGPU.Vector.PathGeometry`, applies the WPF geometry/world transform through `PathGeometry.CreateTransformed(...)`, uses `TryGetBounds(...)`/`ArcSegmentGeometry` for arc-aware bounds, and inflates strokes through `TransformMetrics.GetStrokeScale(...)`. The WPF parser remains reused, but the previous WPF-local endpoint-radius arc box helper was removed so future clipping/cache/layout fixes can continue moving toward backend-owned vector math.
- Moved the real WPF non-Windows `Geometry.GetBoundsHelper(...)` polygon/line fallback onto ProGPU-owned vector helpers too. `ProGPU.Vector.PolygonGeometryBounds` now owns point-span transform, finite-value validation, and transformed stroke inflation through `TransformMetrics`; real `PresentationCore` only marshals the MIL point array to `Vector2` before calling it. This removes the WPF-local `TransformManagedPoint`/`GetManagedStrokeScale` fallback used by TabControl, Xceed, AvalonDock, and DataGrid layout/hit-test precompute paths, while exact geometry point/stroke hit testing remains a later ProGPU vector task.
- Moved the reusable part of real WPF non-Windows generic geometry hit testing onto ProGPU-owned vector helpers. `ProGPU.Vector.BoundsHitTesting` now owns point-in-bounds evaluation plus WPF-style absolute/relative tolerance expansion, and real `PresentationCore.Geometry.ContainsInternal(...)` only adapts WPF `Rect`/`Point` data from the existing path and polygon bounds queries before calling it. The current behavior remains deliberately conservative and bounds-based for popup/input bring-up, but the WPF-local `InflateForHitTolerance`/`Rect.Contains` media fallback has been removed so exact fill/stroke hit testing can be implemented in ProGPU.Vector next.
- Moved real WPF non-Windows `RectangleGeometry.ContainsInternal(...)` fill/stroke containment onto ProGPU-owned vector helpers. `ProGPU.Vector.RectangleGeometryHitTesting` now owns axis-aligned and rounded-rectangle fill checks plus stroke-ring tolerance handling, while real `PresentationCore` only transforms the hit point through the WPF `Transform.Inverse` and adapts `Rect`/`Point`/`Pen` values to `Vector2`. This removes the WPF-local rectangle fill/stroke geometry math that was introduced for input bring-up and keeps Toolkit/DataGrid hit testing on the same reusable ProGPU vector path.
- Moved real WPF non-Windows `EllipseGeometry.ContainsInternal(...)` fill/stroke containment onto ProGPU-owned vector helpers as well. `ProGPU.Vector.EllipseGeometryHitTesting` now owns exact normalized ellipse fill checks plus concentric stroke-ring tolerance handling, and real `PresentationCore` only transforms the hit point through the WPF `Transform.Inverse` before adapting center/radius/pen values. This avoids the previous non-Windows fallback through conservative Bezier-control-point bounds for primitive ellipse hit testing.
- Moved real WPF non-Windows `LineGeometry.ContainsInternal(...)` solid fill/stroke hit testing onto ProGPU-owned vector helpers. `ProGPU.Vector.LineGeometryHitTesting` now owns open-line fill rejection, solid line body distance checks, absolute/relative tolerance expansion, and flat/square/round/triangle cap handling, while real `PresentationCore` only adapts transforms, endpoints, pens, and cap metadata. Dashed line hit testing intentionally remains on the existing fallback until exact dash/stroke containment is moved into ProGPU vector.
- Moved real WPF non-Windows `PathGeometry` fill containment onto ProGPU-owned vector helpers. `ProGPU.Vector.PathGeometryHitTesting` now flattens line, quadratic, cubic, and arc segments into reusable path polygons, applies WPF fill rules (`EvenOdd`/`Nonzero`), handles near-boundary tolerance, and returns an unsupported signal so real `PresentationCore.Geometry.ContainsInternal(...)` can fall back conservatively for stroke/dash/combined cases. WPF still reuses its serialized path parser and adapts `PathGeometryData` into the ProGPU path model, but the filled-path containment decision is no longer a WPF-local bounds box.
- Added the first GPU-native hit-test cache path in ProGPU. `ProGPU.Vector.GpuHitTestPrimitive`, `GpuHitTestIndex`, `GpuHitTestDeviceIndex`, and `GpuHitTestEngine` now define a WebGPU compute-shader query ABI with GPU-resident quadtree node/primitive buffers, world-space broad-phase bounds, inverse local transforms, and precise shader-side rectangle, rounded-rectangle, ellipse, and line stroke/fill tests. `ProGPU.Scene.GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` is fed from the compositor's render-command compile pass, reusing the already processed render command geometry, stroke, fill, transform, opacity, and clip state to build and upload the device-side index once per rendered frame instead of replaying a separate WPF media geometry pass or reuploading the tree per mouse query. `Compositor.LastHitTestIndex`, `Compositor.LastHitTestDeviceIndex`, `Compositor.TryHitTestPoint(...)`, `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.LastGpuHitTestIndex`, `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.LastGpuHitTestDeviceIndex`, and `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.TryHitTestPoint(...)` expose that cache/query surface for the WPF host. The earlier dashed-line CPU helper expansion was dropped from this slice; dashed/path/combined precision should be added as GPU/vector hit-test primitives instead of new managed WPF containment code.
- Added source-owner id plumbing for the GPU hit-test cache. `RenderCommand.HitTestId` now flows into `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` primitive ids, and the retained WPF replay path assigns ids through `WpfGpuHitTestOwnerMap` when `ProGpuRetainedCompositionCommandSink` enters a source-owner scope. `ProGpuCompositionCommandSink` stamps the active id onto native render commands, and `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.TryHitTestOwner(...)` resolves a GPU hit result back to the retained WPF source owner object. This still preserves WPF's visual-tree routing semantics as the next integration step, but it removes the previous blocker where GPU results were only anonymous render-command ids.
- Wired portable mouse hit testing to the GPU owner cache. `PortablePresentationSource` now exposes an internal `HitTestOverride` callback, `WpfPortablePresentationSourceBridge` installs a ProGPU-backed callback for real portable sources, and `MouseDevice.LocalHitTest(...)` asks that callback before falling back to `root.InputHitTest(...)`. The callback uses `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.TryHitTestOwner(...)` and `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.TryHitTestOwner(...)` to resolve the top rendered owner from the GPU-resident hit-test index, while PresentationCore still converts returned dependency objects into WPF enabled/raw input elements. When a current GPU cache exists, the bridge returns a handled miss sentinel for no-owner results so portable mouse input does not fall through to the CPU drawing-content hit-test walk; fallback remains only for startup/no-cache and non-WPF-object cases.
- Extended the GPU-native hit-test cache to path geometry. `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` now compiles `DrawPath` commands into the same ProGPU path segment records used by rendering/path atlas work, stores those segments in `GpuHitTestIndex`, uploads a GPU path-segment buffer beside the quadtree, and emits `PathFill`/`PathStroke` primitives instead of broad bounds-only path hits. The WebGPU hit-test shader now evaluates path fill rules and sampled line/quadratic/cubic/arc stroke spans directly against the cached segment data. This keeps path hit testing on the render-time ProGPU geometry/stroke/fill cache and avoids adding another managed WPF media hit-test pass for normal path visuals.
- Routed the simple public topmost point hit-test overload through the same GPU owner cache. `VisualTreeHelper.HitTest(reference, point)` now asks `PortablePresentationSource.TryPointHitTestOverride(...)` before `reference.HitTest(...)` on portable sources, transforms the query point through the portable root, verifies the GPU-resolved visual belongs to the requested reference subtree, and returns a `PointHitTestResult` without walking WPF drawing content when the current GPU frame can answer. Callback and geometry hit-test overloads remain on WPF's existing recursive path until ProGPU exposes ordered result enumeration.
- Added ordered GPU hit-test result enumeration and routed no-filter WPF point callback hit testing through it. `GpuHitTestEngine.TryHitTestPointAll(...)` uses the existing render-time quadtree, primitive, transform, clip, stroke/fill, and path-segment buffers, stores a bounded z-ordered hit list in a GPU result buffer, and returns those results without replaying WPF drawing content on the CPU. `Compositor.TryHitTestPointAll(...)`, `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.TryHitTestOwners(...)`, and `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.TryHitTestOwners(...)` expose the owner list to `PortablePresentationSource.HitTestAllOverride`; `Visual.HitTest(...)` now bypasses `HitTestPoint(...)` for no-filter point callbacks when the portable GPU cache can answer. Filtered callbacks and geometry hit-test overloads intentionally stay on WPF's recursive path until ProGPU can evaluate user filters and geometry hit regions without violating WPF callback semantics.
- Routed direct WPF `UIElement.InputHitTest(...)` calls through the same ordered GPU owner list on portable sources. `PortablePresentationSource.TryInputHitTestOverride(...)` consumes `HitTestAllOverride`, skips non-descendant and non-input-hit-test-visible owner paths, returns a `PointHitTestResult` for the first eligible visual, and reports handled misses once a GPU cache exists. `UIElement.InputHitTest(...)` now asks that hook before `VisualTreeHelper.HitTest(...)` and shares the original WPF raw/enabled candidate promotion logic through `PromoteInputHit(...)`, so controls such as popup services, date pickers, DataGrid checkbox columns, text editing, and other direct input-hit callers avoid the CPU drawing-content walk after a valid ProGPU frame.
- Tightened ProGPU path hit-test cache precision for unsupported path compilation. `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` no longer converts uncompiled `DrawPath` commands into broad `AxisAlignedBounds` primitives; it catches unsupported path-op compilation failures and skips the path until exact GPU path segments are available. This avoids false-positive hit boxes for incomplete/unsupported combined paths and keeps the portable WPF hit-test route fail-closed instead of reintroducing box-based managed workarounds.
- Routed filtered WPF point callback hit testing through the ordered GPU owner list as well. `Visual.HitTest(...)` now asks `PortablePresentationSource.TryPointHitTestOverride(...)` regardless of whether a `HitTestFilterCallback` is present, and `PortablePresentationSource` applies WPF `HitTestFilterBehavior` over each GPU-resolved visual's ancestor path before invoking the user result callback. That keeps arbitrary user filters and callback behavior in managed PresentationCore while avoiding WPF's recursive drawing-content walk for point callbacks after a valid ProGPU hit-test cache exists. Geometry-region callbacks remain on the existing path until ProGPU exposes non-point region queries.
- Synced ProGPU visual clip scopes into the GPU hit-test cache. The compositor now pushes `Visual.ClipBounds` and outer `ScrollableAreaClip` scopes into `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` when it pushes the matching render clip stack, then pops them with the visual scope. This means Xceed/DataGrid scrolled or viewport-clipped visuals produce clipped GPU broad-phase bounds for input hit testing instead of accepting owners outside the rendered viewport; the fix lives in ProGPU's render compile pass rather than WPF/Xceed control code.
- Preserved GPU hit-test ownership across retained layer/effect caches. `ProGPU.Scene.Visual` now carries a retained `HitTestId`, the WPF retained sink stamps source-owner ids onto owner/cache/effect visuals, and the compositor adds a main-pass texture replay primitive for cached layer/effect outputs while suspending hit-test cache writes during offscreen render passes. Normal geometry, stroke, fill, transform, opacity, clip, and path-segment metadata still comes from render-command compilation, while retained cache reuse no longer loses hit-test owners or pollutes the main frame with offscreen sub-render entries.
- Extended the commercial Xceed paid DataGrid MVP from static surface validation into loaded command-path validation. `PROGPU_WPF_XCEED_PAID_RUN_VALIDATE=1` now drives the real sample handlers for row add, last-row selection, in-memory settings save/load, Status column hide/show through `ColumnBase.Visible`, Tableflow/Cardflow/TableView switching, and editable-grid score validation, then asserts the resulting DataGrid/view-model state. The row-selection helper now explicitly synchronizes `PaidDataGrid.SelectedItem` with the view-model selection, keeping command traffic on normal Xceed/WPF managers while ProGPU continues to own rendering, clipping, input, invalidation, and GPU hit testing.
- Tightened GPU hit-test cache fidelity for dashed path strokes in ProGPU. The render command cache now reuses the compositor's existing dashed-stroke path lowering before compiling `PathStroke` hit-test primitives, so dash gaps are not treated as full solid path hits. The focused GPU hit-test test validates both a dash hit and a gap miss through the WebGPU query path, keeping dashed stroke precision in the backend cache instead of adding managed WPF media hit-test workarounds.
- Added a GPU broad-phase bounds query path on top of the same render-time hit-test cache. `GpuHitTestQuery` now carries a second bounds endpoint, the WebGPU shader has an explicit bounds-query mode with capacity masking, node/primitive bounds intersection, z-ordered result insertion, and visibility filtering, and `GpuHitTestEngine.TryQueryBoundsAll(...)`/`Compositor.TryQueryHitTestBoundsAll(...)` expose the GPU-owned candidate list without replaying WPF drawing content. `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.TryQueryHitTestBoundsOwners(...)` resolves those candidates through the retained owner map for the next geometry-region adapter. The path is intentionally broad-phase only today: point queries still run precise fill/stroke/path tests, while arbitrary WPF `GeometryHitTestParameters` still need shader-side region precision before the remaining recursive CPU geometry callback can be removed safely.
- Routed portable WPF geometry callback hit testing through the GPU bounds-owner candidate path when a ProGPU frame cache is available. `PortablePresentationSource` now exposes `HitTestBoundsOverride`, transforms `GeometryHitTestParameters.Bounds` from the reference visual into portable-root coordinates, calls the ProGPU owner list, applies the same WPF filter-callback ancestor-path semantics used by point callbacks, and returns `GeometryHitTestResult` entries without walking WPF drawing content. `WpfPortablePresentationSourceBridge` installs that hook through reflection and `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.TryQueryHitTestBoundsOwners(...)` forwards to the composition target. This is still a conservative bounds-candidate geometry route with `IntersectionDetail.Intersects`; exact arbitrary region/shape detail remains a ProGPU shader task rather than a reason to add WPF-side media geometry walkers.
- Added first GPU-computed geometry callback intersection detail. ProGPU bounds-query results now use the spare result field as a `GpuHitTestIntersectionDetail`, and the WebGPU shader classifies safe bounds relationships as `FullyInside`, `FullyContains`, or `Intersects` for axis-aligned bounds/rect primitives while leaving non-rectangular shape precision conservative. The WPF bridge now returns neutral ProGPU geometry candidates carrying owner plus detail; `PortablePresentationSource` decodes those candidates reflectively and creates `GeometryHitTestResult` with the mapped WPF `IntersectionDetail`. This improves region callback fidelity without making `ProGPU.Wpf` compile against real PresentationCore hit-test result types or adding WPF-side geometry walkers.
- Tightened the paid Xceed Toolkit/DataGrid sample dependency graph. The SDK-switched paid sample now pins patched direct `System.Data.SqlClient` and `System.Drawing.Common` package versions over Xceed's legacy transitive versions, so `PROGPU_WPF_XCEED_PAID_VALIDATE=1 ./eng/run-progpu-wpf-xceed-paid.sh` restores, builds, and validates the package surface with zero warnings while still loading licenses only from environment variables and leaving the managed Xceed control tree unchanged.
- Reused cached ellipse primitive metadata for GPU bounds/region hit queries. The ProGPU WebGPU hit-test shader now transforms rectangle query bounds into primitive-local space for axis-aligned ellipse fill/stroke primitives, rejects empty ellipse-corner and ellipse-stroke-hole candidates before recording owners, reports `FullyContains` for rectangle regions fully inside an ellipse fill, and counts those checks as precise GPU region tests. Focused GPU tests now cover false-positive rejection, ellipse detail classification, and stroke-hole rejection without adding any WPF-side media geometry walkers.
- Reused cached path segment metadata for GPU bounds/region hit queries. The ProGPU WebGPU hit-test shader now tests rectangular query regions against the same cached path segment buffer used for point-precise path fill/stroke hits, rejects path-fill/path-stroke broad-bounds false positives, conservatively reports `FullyContains` only when a rectangular region is inside a path fill without boundary crossings, and counts those checks as precise GPU region tests. This keeps WPF geometry callbacks on the ProGPU render-time geometry/stroke/fill cache path and avoids redoing path analysis through managed WPF media walkers after a valid GPU frame exists.
- Added a portable bridge regression guard for GPU-cache handled misses. The WPF bridge test now installs an empty ProGPU hit-test cache and asserts that point, ordered point, and bounds override delegates return handled miss sentinels instead of `null`; this prevents a rendered-frame miss from falling through to WPF's CPU drawing-content hit-test walk while preserving startup/no-cache compatibility.
- Locked valid combined/path-op geometry into the GPU hit-test cache contract. Focused ProGPU tests now build a combined difference path with a hole, verify render-command compilation emits cached `PathFill` segment data rather than a broad bounds box, and assert both point and rectangular bounds queries reject hits inside the hole on the WebGPU shader path. Malformed/uncompiled combined paths still fail closed instead of adding owner boxes.
- Reused cached line-stroke primitive metadata for GPU bounds/region hit queries. `GpuHitTestPrimitive` now carries a render-time helper payload for line-stroke direction and segment length, so point and rectangular-region shaders reuse data computed while render commands are already being compiled instead of recalculating it per query. The ProGPU WebGPU hit-test shader now tests rectangular query regions against stroked line bodies and flat/round/square/triangle cap regions, rejects line-stroke broad-bounds false positives including flat-cap overhangs, and counts those checks as precise GPU region tests. This moves another common WPF geometry callback case onto the render-time hit-test cache instead of accepting stroke-inflated boxes or reintroducing managed WPF media hit testing after a valid GPU cache exists.
- Added precise GPU bounds/region checks for cached rectangle fill/stroke primitives. Rounded-rectangle fill queries now reject rounded-corner broad-bounds false positives and can report `FullyContains` when the rectangular query is entirely inside the rounded fill, while rectangle stroke queries reject interior stroke-hole hits. This keeps WPF geometry callbacks on the same render-time primitive cache used for point hit testing instead of replaying managed WPF drawing content for common control chrome and border shapes.
- Added the first non-rectangular GPU region-query mode. `GpuHitTestEngine.TryQueryEllipseAll(...)` uses the existing render-time quadtree/device buffers with an ellipse-region flag, culls broad-phase nodes and primitives against the actual query ellipse instead of the query AABB, and classifies axis-aligned non-rounded rectangle fill/bounds primitives as `Empty`, `FullyInside`, `FullyContains`, or `Intersects` on the shader path. `Compositor.TryQueryHitTestEllipseAll(...)`, `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget.TryQueryHitTestEllipseCandidates(...)`, and `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.TryQueryHitTestEllipseCandidates(...)` expose the backend path for the next portable WPF geometry-adapter step without adding managed drawing-content replay.
- Routed simple WPF ellipse geometry callbacks onto that GPU ellipse-query path. `GeometryHitTestParameters` now records a cheap axis-aligned ellipse query hint before WPF flattens the public geometry to its internal `PathGeometry`, and `PortablePresentationSource` calls the new ellipse override when the reference-to-root transform preserves an axis-aligned query rectangle. `WpfPortablePresentationSourceBridge` binds that override to `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.TryQueryHitTestEllipseCandidates(...)`, so rendered-frame ellipse-region hit tests are answered from the ProGPU cache instead of broad AABB-only candidates or WPF drawing-content CPU replay.
- Cached ellipse center and inverse-radii in the ProGPU hit-test primitive payload during render-command cache construction. The WebGPU hit-test shader now uses those cached values for ellipse fill and stroke point/rectangular-region checks instead of recomputing center/radius normalization from bounds for each query, matching the earlier line-stroke direction/length cache pattern and keeping helper data generation on the render/stroke/fill processing path.
- Tightened ellipse-region GPU queries against cached ellipse primitives. `TryQueryEllipseAll(...)` now rejects proven separated ellipse-fill candidates using cached center/radii data, reports same-center `FullyInside`/`FullyContains` details when radii ordering proves containment, and rejects same-center ellipse-stroke hole hits without falling back to WPF managed geometry replay. Harder arbitrary ellipse/path region relationships remain conservative `Intersects` until exact shader-side region math is added.
- Tightened ellipse-region GPU queries against cached line-stroke primitives too. `GpuHitTestPrimitive.LineStroke(...)` now has an explicit helper-data builder for normalized direction and segment length, render-command cache tests assert `DrawLine` and `DrawEllipse` produce those reusable payloads while rendering is compiled, and the WebGPU ellipse-region shader uses that cached line data to reject broad-bounds false positives without calling WPF drawing-content hit testing. The portable bridge tests now also cover ellipse-region cache misses so point, bounds, and ellipse queries all fail closed after a valid ProGPU cache exists.
- Extended ellipse-region GPU queries to cached path fill and stroke primitives. The WebGPU hit-test shader now tests query ellipses against the same cached `GpuPathSegment` buffer used for point and rectangular-region path hit testing, rejecting difference-path hole queries and path-stroke broad-bounds false positives while conservatively reporting `Intersects` when the sampled path data proves overlap. This keeps non-rectangular WPF geometry callbacks on the render-time path cache instead of falling back to WPF drawing-content replay.
- Extended ellipse-region GPU queries to cached rounded-rectangle fill and rectangle-stroke primitives. The WebGPU hit-test shader decomposes rounded rectangles into center rectangles plus corner ellipses and checks rectangle-stroke outer/inner regions from the cached primitive payload, rejecting rounded-corner and stroke-hole false positives without adding WPF-managed containment boxes or redoing render geometry analysis in PresentationCore.
- Added a GPU result-list overflow signal for ordered hit-test queries. `TryHitTestPointAll(...)`, bounds queries, and ellipse-region queries still return only the caller-provided top-N z-ordered results, but the shader now keeps the summary `Hit` field as the total matched owner count before capacity truncation, so large WPF/Xceed/SciChart visual trees can detect bounded-list truncation without replaying WPF drawing content on the CPU.
- Consumed that GPU overflow signal in the WPF bridge. `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget` now retries point, bounds, and ellipse hit-list queries with a larger GPU result buffer up to the ProGPU backend cap when unmapped top hits hide the first mapped owner or leave the caller's owner/candidate span underfilled. The public WPF override remains bounded, but deeper GPU cache hits can now resolve retained WPF owners without falling back to managed drawing-content hit testing.
- Deduplicated WPF owner resolution over raw GPU hit primitives. The bridge now preserves GPU z-order while returning each retained WPF owner only once for point, bounds, and ellipse candidate lists, so common fill+stroke or multi-primitive visuals cannot consume the bounded WPF callback span and hide deeper distinct owners. When duplicate primitives underfill the distinct-owner list, the same GPU overflow signal triggers the larger-buffer retry path instead of falling back to CPU media hit testing.
- Moved duplicate-id suppression into the native ProGPU hit-list shader too. `GpuHitTestEngine` now keeps `summary.Hit` as the raw matched primitive count for overflow diagnostics, but the stored point/bounds/ellipse result list is distinct by primitive id and keeps the highest-z primitive for that id. Readback counts actual stored records, so duplicate fill/stroke primitives cannot consume the native top-N result capacity before WPF owner mapping runs.
- Removed the WPF bridge-local duplicate-owner scan from GPU hit result mapping. `ProGpuWpfCompositionTarget` now trusts the native ProGPU distinct-id list and only resolves ids back to retained WPF owners/candidates, keeping duplicate suppression in the render/GPU cache path instead of redoing it in managed WPF hit-test code.
- Fixed the paid Xceed Toolkit/DataGrid MVP validation against the installed commercial package versions. The sample now uses `ColumnStretchMode="All"` for Xceed DataGrid 7.3, wires the Windows10 theme licenser from the existing Toolkit license environment variable, documents and directly references `Xceed.Wpf.Themes.Windows10`, keeps construct-only validation away from loaded template/current-row state, and passes both `PROGPU_WPF_XCEED_PAID_VALIDATE=1` and `PROGPU_WPF_XCEED_PAID_RUN_VALIDATE=1` with license variables supplied from the environment.
- Shared render-time path compilation data with the GPU hit-test cache. `PathAtlas` now keeps a bounded content-hash cache of compiled `GpuPathRecord`/`GpuPathSegment` payloads, reuses those payloads for atlas allocation/rasterization, and exposes them to `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` through a small compilation-cache interface. The compositor wires its existing atlas into the hit-test cache builder, so `DrawPath` hit-test primitives consume the same backend-owned path/stroke/fill helper data prepared for rendering instead of recompiling paths or falling back to WPF managed geometry walkers.
- Moved path hit-test cache production more explicitly onto the render compilation path. `Compositor.CompilePathCommand(...)` now prewarms the shared `PathAtlas` hit-test payload cache for fill and stroke paths, and normal draw commands are added to the GPU hit-test builder after render lowering while clip/opacity state commands still update the cache stack before drawing. Focused ProGPU tests now assert a precompiled path payload is consumed without recompilation, and dashed `DrawLine` commands lower to GPU `PathStroke` primitives through the same dashed-stroke path expansion used by rendering instead of accepting a solid full-line hit box.
- Hardened the paid Xceed validation runner. `eng/run-progpu-wpf-xceed-paid.sh` now imports `XCEED_TOOLKIT_LICENSE_KEY` and `XCEED_DATAGRID_LICENSE_KEY` from macOS `launchctl getenv` when the current shell does not contain them, without printing or storing values. `PROGPU_WPF_XCEED_PAID_RUN_VALIDATE=1` now fails fast when loaded-window validation still lacks licenses instead of opening the missing-license UI and hanging CI/manual validation.
- Moved ProGPU `DrawPolyline` hit testing off broad bounds and onto the same path-stroke primitive cache used for exact path hits. `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` now reads array-backed and provider/point-buffer-backed polyline commands from the render command stream, wraps them as lightweight `PathGeometry` figures, preserves closed figures and dashed pens through the existing native dashed-stroke path expansion, and emits `PathStroke` hit primitives. The compositor now passes the active render data provider into hit-test cache writes, so WPF/Xceed/SciChart chart polylines can reject empty-space hits inside their old bounding boxes without adding managed WPF media hit-test code.
- Moved ProGPU `FillTriangle` and `FillQuad` hit testing off broad bounds as well. Filled triangles now emit precise `PathFill` primitives, and filled quads emit the same two triangle `PathFill` primitives that the renderer submits, preserving non-rectangular and concave quad behavior while native result-list deduplication keeps both primitives mapped to the same owner id. Focused GPU tests now prove points inside the old triangle/quad bounding boxes but outside the real filled area are rejected on the WebGPU hit-test path.
- Fed `GpuPicture` playback into the render-time GPU hit-test cache. `Compositor.CompilePicture(...)` now mirrors normal visual playback by pushing picture-local clip/opacity state into `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` before rendering each child command and adding child draw commands afterward with the `GpuPicture` data provider, so recorded/cached picture content is no longer visually rendered but absent from GPU owner/candidate queries. A headless compositor regression now draws a clipped picture-contained point-buffer polyline and asserts the last GPU hit-test index contains the clipped `PathStroke` primitive.
- Moved quadratic and cubic Bezier render commands into the same GPU path-stroke hit-test lane. `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` now wraps `DrawBezier` and `DrawCubicBezier` commands as lightweight `PathGeometry` figures with native quadratic/cubic path segments, reuses the existing dashed-path lowering for dashed pens, and emits `PathStroke` primitives instead of omitting rendered curves from the cache. Focused GPU tests now cover quadratic, cubic, and dashed Bezier cache construction plus WebGPU point-hit rejection for empty space inside the old curve bounds.
- Added command-level geometry helper caching for render/hit-test reuse. `RenderCommandGeometryCache` now carries reusable stroke/fill helper paths for recorded line, path, polyline, triangle, quad, and Bezier commands, memoizes dashed-stroke lowering with a mutable-pen signature, and is consumed by both compositor path compilation and `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder`. Translated `DrawingContext.Append(...)` copies invalidate stale caches, while focused tests assert recorded dashed-line and Bezier commands hit the shared path compiler without rebuilding wrapper paths. This keeps helper data in ProGPU's render-command path and avoids reintroducing WPF-managed CPU geometry hit-test boxes.
- Closed the `DrawCircle` render/hit-test mismatch in ProGPU. Circles now lower into the same cached ellipse fill/stroke GPU hit-test primitives used by rendered ellipses, including center and inverse-radius helper data plus stroke-expanded broad-phase bounds. Focused tests now cover circle cache metadata and WebGPU point rejection in the old square bounds corner.
- Moved spline stroke hit testing onto the same render-time ProGPU geometry cache path. `DrawingContext.DrawSpline(...)` now records a cached max-detail spline stroke path, `SplineExtensionPipeline` and hit-test cache construction share the same `SplineGeometry` evaluator, stale duplicate B-spline evaluation code was removed from `Compositor`, and `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` now emits `PathStroke` primitives for spline `DrawExtension` commands from either cached command data or provider buffers. Focused GPU tests cover inline spline commands, recorded-cache reuse, provider fallback, and WebGPU point hits so rendered spline strokes no longer require WPF-managed geometry replay or broad owner boxes.
- Added GPU hit-test coverage for ProGPU chart-series extension commands. `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` now consumes provider float buffers and `GpuSeriesBuffer.CachedInterleaved` data for `GpuLineSeries` and `GpuScatterSeries`, lowering high-volume line series into chunked `PathStroke` primitives and scatter markers into ellipse-fill primitives while preserving scale/translate and NaN line gaps. Immediate series commands now record identity scale/translate explicitly. Focused GPU tests cover metadata construction, static cached buffers, chunking, null gaps, and WebGPU point hits/misses, so chart-heavy WPF/Xceed/SciChart MVP paths can use the render-time ProGPU cache instead of managed WPF hit boxes.
- Finished the current GPU hit-test/input correctness slice for SDK-switched WPF apps. ProGPU compositor visual-tree compilation now emits retained visual owner bounds into the GPU hit-test cache, so WPF controls with no immediate draw primitive still participate in owner queries through the same native quadtree/result buffers as rendered geometry. The WPF retained visual traversal now preserves real visual size/content/clip bounds instead of inheriting broad parent sizes, and package-mode size/bounds probing avoids compile-time WPF type identity traps.
- Tightened portable WPF owner selection over GPU hit results. `WpfPortablePresentationSourceBridge` now ignores transparent adorner overlays, normalizes through template/layout infrastructure, and selects the deepest normalized GPU owner. This keeps non-focusable capture controls such as `Thumb` ahead of focusable ancestors, while also allowing nested Toolkit/AvalonDock editors to win over broad overlay owners. The bridge still fails closed after a valid GPU cache exists rather than falling back to WPF drawing-content CPU hit testing.
- Fixed GPU hit-test cache freshness without reentrant render flushes. `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` refreshes stale cache data before external hit-test queries, but now skips synchronous render wakeup while native input is already being forwarded into WPF. This prevents WPF mouse-capture hit testing from forcing a nested render/dispatcher flush while dispatcher processing is suspended, while preserving the current GPU cache for input routing.
- Removed Toolkit live validation's CPU `InputHitTest` dependency for click preflight. The Toolkit sample now checks `ProGpuWpfWindowHost.TryHitTestOwners(...)` through the live host and only keeps WPF `InputHitTest` as diagnostic text, aligning the sample with the project rule that rendered-frame input should be GPU-owner driven rather than WPF media hit-test driven.
- Revalidated the SDK sample matrix after the hit-test fixes and refreshed local `11.0.0-dev` packages. Passing commands: focused `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` bridge/activation tests, `PROGPU_WPF_HELLO_LIVE_VALIDATE=1 ./eng/run-progpu-wpf-hello.sh`, MVP live and Application.Run validations, Toolkit Application.Run and full live validation including 100k DataGrid virtualization/AvalonDock, `PROGPU_WPF_XCEED_PAID_RUN_VALIDATE=1 ./eng/run-progpu-wpf-xceed-paid.sh`, and SciChart MVP self-test/Application.Run validations. The full WPF-app MVP remains an SDK-switched apphost lane, not a full arbitrary WPF app compatibility claim yet.
- Tightened the GPU hit-test cache for geometry clips directly in ProGPU. `GpuHitTestPrimitive` now carries active clip path segment metadata, `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` compiles `PushGeometryClip` paths once while the compositor is already processing render commands, preserves that metadata through nested rectangular clips, and stamps affected primitives with the clip range. The WebGPU hit-test shader now rejects point, rectangular-region, and ellipse-region hits outside the active clip path by reusing the same cached `GpuPathSegment` buffer as normal path fill/stroke queries. Focused ProGPU validation passes `GpuHitTestingTests` with 87 tests, WPF bridge/owner tests pass with 59 tests, and MVP plus Toolkit `Application.Run` validations still pass. A broad `FullyQualifiedName~Composition` WPF test probe still exposes unrelated retained-renderer baseline expectation failures and was not treated as part of this backend hit-test slice.
- Extended GPU geometry-clip hit testing through nested arbitrary clip intersections. `GpuRenderCommandHitTestCacheBuilder` now keeps the active clip path in the clip stack and, when a second `PushGeometryClip` is encountered, builds a ProGPU combined-path intersection before compiling the clip segments for affected primitives. This keeps nested clip precision in the same render-time path-op/cache pipeline used by normal path rendering and avoids managed WPF owner boxes for clipped Toolkit/DataGrid content. Validation passed `dotnet build src/ProGPU.Tests/ProGPU.Tests.csproj --no-restore --verbosity minimal`, `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major dotnet vstest src/ProGPU.Tests/bin/Debug/net10.0/ProGPU.Tests.dll --TestCaseFilter:FullyQualifiedName~GpuHitTestingTests` with 88 tests, focused `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` bridge/drawing tests with 59 tests, and MVP plus Toolkit `Application.Run` validations.
- Finished the current portable input/GPU owner-routing fix for SDK-switched apps. The WPF bridge now filters transparent `AdornerLayer`/`AdornerDecorator` owners out of the GPU all-hits override and skips them during pointer-owner normalization, so `UIElement.InputHitTest(...)` and raw mouse routing resolve the rendered client target instead of the root adorner infrastructure. The external no-source-change SDK smoke now validates live mouse input through a normal client-area probe, while `PortableWindowActivationService` guards custom-chrome edge coordinates by clamping negative device-client values only when the original root point is WPF-hit-testable. Validation passed focused `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` bridge/window/input/render tests, external no-source-change SDK smoke, `./eng/progpu-wpf-mvp-quickcheck.sh`, Toolkit/AvalonDock validation, paid Xceed validation, and SciChart MVP validation.
- Stabilized the paid Xceed Toolkit/DataGrid app path after the latest rendering/crash pass. `ProGpuWpfWindowHost` now ignores late platform input/render wakeups during disposal and treats dispatcher-suspended render wakeups as deferred instead of crashing; `WpfPortableWindowActivation` similarly fail-closes suspended dispatcher flushes. The retained visual replay now synthesizes `ClipToBounds` rectangle clips from render size without directly loading WPF `Rect`/`RectangleGeometry` in package mode, preserves render-size retained bounds for real visual slots, and fills missing local clips for Xceed DataGrid cell-like retained visuals from their arranged size so cell content stays bounded by the ProGPU retained scene clip path. Focused `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` build, cleaned `ProGPU.Wpf` package generation, and `PROGPU_WPF_XCEED_PAID_VALIDATE=1 PROGPU_WPF_XCEED_PAID_RUN_VALIDATE=1 DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major ./eng/run-progpu-wpf-xceed-paid.sh` pass. - Recorded the reflection-free porting requirement in root `agents.md` and the ProGPU branch plan. Runtime reflection in the WPF bridge and ProGPU support code is now explicitly treated as temporary scaffolding; after the current paid Xceed stabilization, the next cleanup priority is typed/generated/source-integrated WPF/MIL/resource/visual access plus ProGPU-native rendering, text, clipping, hit-test, DirectX, and platform primitives without managed bridge workarounds.
- Started the reflection-free bridge cleanup with a typed portable presentation source contract. Real `PresentationCore` and the ProGPU compile-time shim now expose `IPortablePresentationSourceHost`, `PortablePresentationSource` implements it, and the bridge no longer needs shape reflection for root, handle, composition target, DPI/client-size sync, render/cursor events, or GPU hit-test override installation. The hit-test callback contract intentionally uses primitive double coordinates rather than WPF `Point` so package-mode ProGPU.Wpf does not bind to shim-owned `PresentationCore` value types while real WPF resolves `Point` from `WindowsBase`. Portable source creation now goes through `PortablePresentationSourceHost.Create(...)`, cursor updates use the typed `RequestedCursorName`, and WPF owner routing uses a new `IPortableVisualOwnerHost`/`PortableVisualOwnerKind` contract implemented by `UIElement`, `Window`, layout/template infrastructure controls, and adorner surfaces. - Kept source-tree real-WPF validation aligned with the reflection-free bridge direction by fixing the harness load-context model instead of restoring a production cross-context adapter. `ProGPU.Wpf.RealXamlRuntimeHarness` and `ProGPU.Wpf.RealThemeRuntimeHarness` now load `ProGPU.Wpf.dll` into the same custom `AssemblyLoadContext` as real `PresentationCore`/`PresentationFramework`, so `PortablePresentationSourceHost.Create(...)` resolves to the real WPF factory and `Window.Show()` stays on the ProGPU portable activation path instead of falling through to macOS `user32.dll` P/Invokes. Harness-only reflection remains for validating internal WPF/ProGPU state, including synthetic input event creation and retained visual replay, but the product `WpfPortablePresentationSourceBridge` remains typed. - Removed the reflective render-data provider bridge from the hot path. Real `PresentationCore` and the ProGPU shim now expose `IPortableRenderDataDrawingContextSink` plus `PortableRenderDataDrawingContextSinkProvider`; `WpfRenderDataSinkProviderBridge` calls that typed provider directly instead of discovering `RenderDataDrawingContextSinkProvider` by `Assembly`/`Type`, building expression delegates, and invoking methods reflectively. Real WPF `ObjectRenderDataDrawingContextSink` now forwards every render-data instruction to the typed portable sink interface instead of caching `MethodInfo` and using `Invoke(...)` per draw call. `WpfObjectRenderDataDrawingContext` implements the shared sink contract, so object render-data dispatch remains package-mode compatible while the production bridge is reflection-free. Harness-only emitted proxies cover old custom-ALC real `PresentationCore` smoke registration without restoring a production cross-context adapter. Validation passed ProGPU shim restore/build, real `PresentationCore` build, clean `ProGPU.Wpf.Tests` build, 78 focused render-data/frame/generator tests, direct real XAML runtime smoke, real `PresentationCore` render-data provider smoke, and paid Xceed validation. The old code-only `ProGPU.Wpf.RealPresentationFrameworkHarness` still fails before render-data registration at its custom-load portable activation step; the same-context real XAML runtime harness is the validated real `PresentationFramework` path for typed bridge contracts.
- Removed another command-sink reflection fallback from shim geometry rendering. ProGPU now exposes `ProGPU.Scene.INativePathGeometrySource`; the shim `System.Windows.Media.Geometry` implements it explicitly by forwarding to its existing native `TryGetPathGeometry(...)` path. `ProGpuCompositionCommandSink` now uses that interface when package-mode shim geometries can provide a native path, instead of reflecting for a shim-only `Geometry.Draw(DrawingContext, Brush, Pen)` method and invoking it into a temporary recording context. Real WPF path/segment object-shape adaptation remains a tracked transitional seam until a typed/generated real-WPF geometry accessor is available.
- Tightened the same command-sink geometry transition path by removing `System.Reflection` and non-public `BindingFlags` usage from `ProGpuCompositionCommandSink`. The remaining real-WPF geometry object-shape adapter reads only public WPF geometry properties until the port has a source-integrated real-WPF path export; shim geometries stay on the typed `INativePathGeometrySource` path.
- Finished the source-integrated real-WPF geometry export and removed the remaining command-sink geometry object-shape reader. A new signed `ProGPU.Wpf.Interop` submodule assembly defines neutral `IPortableGeometryPathSource`/`PortableGeometryPath` DTOs, source-built real `PresentationCore.Geometry` implements that interface, and `PortableGeometryPathExporter` exports path figures, line/quadratic/cubic/arc segments, transforms, bounds, fill rules, and combined-geometry operation trees. `ProGpuCompositionCommandSink` now consumes shim `INativePathGeometrySource` or real WPF `IPortableGeometryPathSource` only, applies every DTO node's local transform before parent/global transforms, and no longer uses `System.Reflection`, `BindingFlags`, public `GetProperty(...)`, or reflected draw invocation for geometry conversion. The custom SDK package graph, CI pack script, and SDK smoke harnesses now ship and validate `ProGPU.Wpf.Interop` as a signed ProGPU package. - Removed reflection from the Silk.NET monitor/DPI service. `SilkNetWpfMonitorService` now uses only typed `IMonitor` members by default and accepts an explicit `Func<IMonitor, double?>` DPI-scale provider for platform-specific monitor scale data instead of probing arbitrary `DpiScale`, `Scale`, `ContentScale`, `DpiX`, or similar property names with `BindingFlags`. Monitor scale still falls back to Silk.NET video-mode resolution divided by monitor bounds when no valid typed scale is supplied. - Continued the reflection-free resource cleanup with typed solid brush and pen contracts. `ProGPU.Wpf.Interop` now exposes `IPortableBrushSource`/`PortableBrush` and `IPortablePenSource`/`PortablePen`; the ProGPU shim and source-built real WPF `SolidColorBrush`/`Pen` implement those seams; and `WpfResourceResolver` now uses portable brush/pen paths before transitional reflective fallbacks.
